papers.title: Persistence of conormal analyticity for the Euler equations in the half-space
papers.abstract: We prove the persistence of conormal analyticity through the $H^r$ norm, with $r \geq 4$, for the 3D incompressible Euler equations in the half-space $Ω= \mathbb{R}_+^3$. We also establish a lower bound on the radius of conormal analyticity which depends on $\|u\|_{H^r}$ and initial data. In particular, persistence is established in both of the spaces $X_τ^{\rm co}$ and $A_τ^{\rm co}$, the former being based on the conormal operator $Z_k = φ^k \partial_3^k$ and the latter being based on $L^k = (φ\partial_3)^k$. Finally, we show that the norms $\|\cdot \|_{X_τ^{\rm co}}$ and $\|\cdot \|_{A_τ^{\rm co}}$ are equivalent up to a small loss in radius, the proof of which uses explicit identities relating the two conormal operators.

papers.title: PotentialEP: Backprop-Free Training of CIFAR-Scale Generative Models via Equilibrium Propagation
papers.abstract: Generating an image with a diffusion or flow-matching model typically involves integrating a velocity field for hundreds of sequential steps. That computation suits a GPU poorly and an analog neuromorphic substrate well, where one fast, low-power physical relaxation could replace the whole sequence. Two things are needed: a generative algorithm whose computation is a relaxation, and a way to train it without backpropagation, whose global gradient transport is hard to realise in analog. Energy Matching supplies the first, sampling by gradient-descent relaxation on a time-independent potential - but obtaining the gradient that descent follows is itself a backward pass, once per integration step. We prove that a predictive coding network with a single linear injection term added to its energy relaxes to a state whose visible layer carries that gradient inherently, with an error that vanishes for small injection strengths. An Energy Matching model trained by backpropagation can therefore be loaded into this network unchanged and sampled by relaxation alone, matching the original model's FID to within 0.04 at CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-32 scale. The network can also be trained without backpropagation: Equilibrium Propagation reproduces backpropagation's parameter updates to a cosine similarity of 0.9998, and training end to end with those updates reaches an FID of 3.64 on unconditional CIFAR-10 against 3.54 for backpropagation. To our knowledge this is the first CIFAR-10 generative model trained with Equilibrium Propagation, and the first at competitive quality by any backpropagation-free rule. This quality does not require group normalisation or attention: an architecture of only convolutions and pointwise nonlinearities, both native to an analog crossbar, reaches an FID of 3.51 when trained by backpropagation.

papers.title: RADIUS-Assisted Companion PSK Discovery: Enabling WPA3-SAE in Externally Authenticated Multi-PSK (ePSK / MPSK / DPSK / iPSK / PPSK) Deployments
papers.abstract: Large multi-dwelling unit (MDU), student-housing and hospitality networks rarely store resident pre-shared keys (PSKs) on the access point (AP). Instead, the per-resident keys of ePSK, MPSK, DPSK, iPSK or PPSK services are held in an external RADIUS server or cloud database synchronised with the property-management system. Our earlier work, Companion-BSSID-Assisted PSK Discovery (CAPD), brought WPA3-SAE to multi-PSK networks by learning the client's PSK on a WPA2-only companion BSSID and steering the client with IEEE 802.11v to a hidden WPA2/WPA3 primary BSSID of the same SSID. CAPD assumes that the AP can test every PSK itself. This paper removes that assumption. We propose RADIUS-Assisted Companion PSK Discovery (RA-CAPD). The AP forwards the ANonce, the raw EAPOL-Key message 2 (SNonce, MIC, RSNE), the SSID, the client MAC, the BSSID and the AP MAC to the external server in RADIUS vendor-specific attributes (VSAs). The server validates the MIC against all provisioned keys, identifies the matching PSK, and returns it encrypted under the RADIUS shared secret (or a per-AP key for cloud databases), together with the unit, room or user identity and the VLAN. The AP binds the client to this PSK and identity, synchronises the binding across all APs in the domain, and moves the client to the configured profile: 802.11v-capable clients via a BSS Transition Management request, and other clients by disconnection and reconnection. On that profile, SAE-capable clients complete WPA3-SAE and WPA2-only clients complete WPA2-PSK, both with the learned key and no further search, so the companion BSSID serves only for onboarding. We present the design, attribute dictionary, algorithms, complexity and security properties, together with laboratory validation on commercial access points.

papers.title: The GHZ Game in Black and White
papers.abstract: We show that it is possible for three people to win the GHZ game with just the standard real valued misty state formalism, but each party will need to have two balls instead of one. That is, there will be six balls involved, rather than three. In fact, as a general rule, instead of using complex numbers in a quantum computer you can always add a qubit to "tag" complex numbers. But for proofs of non-locality, like the GHZ game, we cannot have a single universal tagging qubit, because all three parties would need access to it and therefore they could potentially transfer information via it. That's where we need to replace the one ball with three that each only need to be accessed locally.

papers.title: Latent Diffusion Modeling of Two- and Three-dimensional Fracture Networks with Sparse Observation Conditioning
papers.abstract: Characterizing subsurface fracture networks is challenging because geometry and connectivity are sparsely observed and uncertain away from measurements. We develop a latent diffusion framework for unconditional and observation-conditioned generation of two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) fracture networks. Fractures and the surrounding matrix are represented as binary fields and compressed by a variational autoencoder into compact spatial latent representations, where an Elucidated Diffusion Model learns their distribution. The 3D model operates on native volumetric fields, with a reconstruction objective designed to preserve sparse, thin fracture structures. Sparse borehole observations are incorporated through a conditioning encoder, classifier-free guidance, and diffusion posterior sampling. Generated ensembles reproduce key fracture-network statistics, including fracture area/volume fraction, two-point correlation, and chord-length distributions. Reconstructed fracture counts and gas-production responses are comparable to those of the reference networks under the considered multiphase flow scenarios. Conditional generation satisfies 99.6% of prescribed well observations in 2D. In 3D, where vertical boreholes constrain full voxel columns, conditional realizations satisfy 84.2% of observed well voxels while maintaining fracture volume and geometry comparable to the reference ensemble. These results demonstrate the potential of latent diffusion models as compact probabilistic representations for fracture-network characterization, ensemble generation, and sparse-observation conditioning.

papers.title: Coarse-Graining Recursive Expert Computation: Continuation-Relative Interfaces and Failure Modes
papers.abstract: Computational coarse-graining aims to replace a sequence of updates with a cheaper module while preserving task performance. We present a continuation-relative evaluation framework that assesses replacements through the computation that follows them, using downstream task quality and total execution cost as joint criteria. The framework distinguishes boundary representations, summaries of skipped computation, executed operations, and downstream loss. It makes interfaces and permitted deployment information explicit, combines fine-path references with directly trained controls using the same shortened architecture, and accounts for selection overhead. An exact loss decomposition separates replacement effects at a fixed downstream action from effects of changing that action. A finite construction shows how retained information can reduce the stipulated cost of zero-error prediction under fixed information and controller restrictions. Experiments in two frozen pretrained language models show that representation fidelity and task loss can favor different fitting objectives. In a prespecified comparison on a 1.7-billion-parameter model, next-token-loss training lowers in-distribution negative log-likelihood by 0.1901 nats per scored token compared with reconstructing the skipped blocks' output, using the same optimizer and update count. This ranking reverses in all nine paired comparisons under distribution shift. In a recursive expert prototype, the jointly adapted candidate lowers task error relative to frozen-bank and router-only baselines, but trails directly trained controls, and the tested input-only selectors fail the joint quality-cost criteria. Together, the protocol and studies provide explicit criteria and diagnostics for distinguishing useful computational replacement from local approximation gains within specified interfaces and evaluation settings.

papers.title: Prior-Informed Generalizable Low-Rank Representation Learning via Regularized Adversarial Reweighting
papers.abstract: Modern learning problems increasingly leverage data from heterogeneous sources to improve robustness and generalizability under distribution shift, often with high-dimensional parameters admitting low-rank structure. Existing group distributionally robust optimization (group-DRO) approaches optimize against adverse source mixtures, but extending this principle to low-rank matrix estimation with a broad class of losses leads to a challenging nonconvex-concave problem for which methods and theory remain limited. We propose Prior-Informed generalizable Low-rank representation Learning via Adversarial Reweighting (PILLAR), which smooths the group-DRO objective by regularizing adversarial source weights toward a user-specified reference distribution while learning a shared low-rank representation. By tempering extreme adversarial reweighting, PILLAR improves estimation stability and reduces the potential conservativeness of group-DRO. Using Burer-Monteiro factorization, we optimize the nonconvex-concave objective by bifactored gradient descent with mirror ascent. We establish linear convergence to a statistical neighborhood of the population saddle point and derive an error bound that separates low-rank estimation from adversarial reweighting. We further show that PILLAR improves on vanilla group DRO when the latter's excess conservativeness dominates source heterogeneity and prior misspecification. Simulations and an electronic health record study of suicide-attempt risk demonstrate improved worst-source and transported predictive accuracy.

papers.title: Red-Teaming of Vision-Language-Action Models via Quality Diversity Environment Generation
papers.abstract: A long-standing goal in robotics is to develop generalist robots that can perform tasks across a wide range of settings, flexibly specified with images and text. Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models offer a promising path toward this goal by training on large collections of robot demonstrations. However, while VLAs perform well in-distribution, they often fail under minor test-time shifts, such as changes in object positions, lighting, textures, and camera poses. To address this, we propose Quality Diversity for Diverse Environment Generation (Q-DEG), a method for improving VLA robustness by generating adversarial environments and fine-tuning the VLA on its own successful rollouts. Q-DEG uses Quality Diversity (QD) optimization to find a set of high-failure environments, while promoting diversity using policy embeddings extracted from the VLA. These environments expose vulnerabilities that can be mitigated through self-imitation fine-tuning, thereby improving the VLA's robustness. In simulation, we conduct experiments across three representative VLA models, and our results indicate that Q-DEG improves robustness to out-of-distribution (OOD) adversarial environments compared to the base VLA and VLAs fine-tuned using data collected from two red-teaming baselines. Furthermore, we demonstrate that improving VLA robustness through Q-DEG facilitates sim-to-real transfer. Our anonymous project website is at: https://qd-env.github.io/qdeg/.

papers.title: Error Bounds and a Smoothing Penalty Method for Binary Orthogonal Optimization
papers.abstract: Binary orthogonal optimization arises in semantic hashing, orthogonal binary projection, and Hadamard matrix design. Existing methods often handle binarity and orthogonality separately, so their outputs need not satisfy both constraints simultaneously and generally come without a residual-based guarantee of exact feasibility. Using an exact box-constrained reformulation, we establish local and global Lipschitz error bounds and prove that the Lipschitz exponent is optimal. In particular, when the binary orthogonal feasible set is nonempty, any box-constrained matrix whose orthogonality residual is below $1$ admits a feasible sign rounding, and the rounding distance is bounded by this residual. These bounds also yield a globally exact nonsmooth orthogonality-residual penalty over the box and a uniformly sharp local penalty threshold. We further develop a smoothing penalty method for binary orthogonal optimization (SPBO). We prove that every accumulation point is stationary for the limiting nonsmooth penalty problem. Numerical experiments on orthogonal binary projection, supervised hashing, and Hadamard completion show that SPBO substantially reduces orthogonality violations while retaining competitive objective values or retrieval accuracy.

papers.title: A Nullstellensatz for the field of complex Laurent series
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be the theory of the valued field of complex Laurent series $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$ in the language of rings expanded by a constant for $t$ and by predicates for $n$-th powers. We introduce a $t$-adic analogue of Kochen's operator, namely $γ(x)=x/(1+tx^{2})$, and the associated Kochen ring $Λ_{L}$ of a field extension $L$ of a model $K$ of $T$. Our main result characterizes the field extensions of $K$ which embed into a model of $T$ (the formally $T$-adic} fields): $L$ is formally $T$-adic if and only if $1/t\notinΛ_{L}$. As an application we prove a Nullstellensatz for $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$: a polynomial $f\in K[X_{1},\dots,X_{n}]$ vanishes on the zero set of an ideal $I$ if and only if $f^{m}=\sum_{i}ω_{i}f_{i}$ for some $m\geqslant 1$, generators $f_{i}$ of $I$ and coefficients $ω_{i}$ in the ring $Λ_{K(X)}\cdot K[X]$. We derive the resulting correspondence between $R$-ideals and algebraic sets, and we compare natural incarnations of the associated $T$-spectrum: prime ideals, morphisms into models of $T$, and the space of types of $T$.

papers.title: Yang-Mills Theory in the Multisymplectic Framework
papers.abstract: This Master's thesis develops and applies the multisymplectic field-theory framework to (pure) Yang-Mills theory. Building from the geometric foundations of jet bundles and the Poincaré-Cartan forms, the work constructs the Lagrangian multisymplectic formalism for first-order field theories, recovering the usual Euler-Lagrange field equations and extending the Poisson brackets of symplectic mechanics to a full graded Lie algebra. It then establishes the Legendre correspondence with the multisymplectic Hamiltonian formalism (in which Hamilton equations are retrieved) including the case of singular Lagrangians (where a constraint algorithm is reproduced). Breaking Lorentz covariance via a Cauchy surface slicing, the thesis then relates the covariant multisymplectic picture to an instantaneous presymplectic (infinite-dimensional) formulation in which the instantaneous De Donder equations and presymplectic brackets are obtained in a compatible way. A comprehensive treatment of symmetries then leads to multisymplectic and instantaneous momentum maps generalizations and to several versions of Noether's theorems. Specializing the formalism to principal-bundle gauge theory, the thesis identifies the multisymplectic configuration space with the bundle of connections, gauge symmetries with symmetries in the multisymplectic language and builds the Yang-Mills Lagrangian. Lastly, among many computations, the standard tensorial Yang-Mills equations and the Bianchi identity in local trivializations are retrieved, Yang-Mills conserved currents and charges are obtained and the graded algebra is derived for a special class of Hamiltonian forms.

papers.title: HoldSpec: A Machine-Checked Model and Conformance Suite for the Payment Authorization Hold Lifecycle
papers.abstract: When a merchant authorizes a card and captures the funds later, the money sits in a state that neither party fully controls: held on the cardholder's account, not yet taken, and due to lapse on a deadline set by the card network. What a merchant may do to that hold, capture part of it, capture again, void it, raise it, let it expire, is business logic that every payment service provider implements slightly differently and none of them specifies formally. We give the lifecycle a state machine in TLA+, parameterized by a provider capability profile, and check eight safety invariants and three liveness properties over 6 profiles, five of them built from Stripe's and Adyen's published documentation. From the same machine we generate a conformance suite that runs black-box against a provider API. Against 61 seeded defects that are distinguishishable from a correct implementation, the generated suite detects 100%, where random sequences with the same call budget reach 56% and a hand-written integration suite reaches 69%; random sequences given ten times the budget still reach only 67%. Running the same suite between two providers turns the comparison into a search, and it returns short executable witnesses for divergences the two documentation sets imply but neither states, including one that breaks the common assumption that a single adapter interface can sit over both, because closing a hold and releasing its remainder is a capture on one provider and a cancel on the other. We report what we could not do: no provider sandbox credentials were available, so every result here concerns documented behavior, and the suite that would test the providers themselves is part of what we release.

papers.title: Flat and Ghost dimensions in tensor triangulated categories with a compact tilting generator
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a tensor triangulated category with a compact tilting generator $M$ and abelian heart $\mathcal{H}_M = M^{\bot_{\neq0}}$. We define a triangulated flat dimension $\mathrm{flatdim}_{\mathcal{T}}X$ for $X\in\mathcal{T}$, and give criteria in terms of tensor vanishing and resolutions by the class of pure quotients of $\mathrm{Add}(M)$. We further introduce $M$-ghost length and $M$-ghost dimension, and show that the global dimension of $\mathcal{H}_M$ controls the $M$-ghost length of all objects in $\mathcal{T}$, and that the $M$-ghost dimension of $\mathcal{T}$ coincides with the weak global dimension of $\mathcal{H}_M$ and the supremum of $\mathrm{flatdim}_{\mathcal{T}}X+\mathrm{inf}X$ of bounded objects, and the relative triangulated dimension of $\mathcal{T}^c$ with respect to $\mathrm{add}(M)$. This extends the classical Hovey-Lockridge theorem, which is recovered for derived categories of rings.

papers.title: A framework for spanning forest identities
papers.abstract: Identities of spanning forest polynomials can come from determinantal identities such as the classical Dodgson identity. They can also be useful in quantum field theory calculations, particularly the quadratic ones. To better understand the structure of spanning forest polynomial identities, we look at when identities on a given graph are generic for all graphs, we ask about dimensions of spaces of spanning forest identities indexed by certain parameters, and we set up a framework that we hope will be helpful for further progress in these directions. As part of this framework, we identify a family of maps naturally given by the all-minors matrix-tree theorem, and we show that their ranks are counted by the Narayana numbers via explicit construction of bases.

papers.title: Absolute moments of GH distribution
papers.abstract: In this work, we focus on deriving the absolute moments of the general ized hyperbolic (GH) distribution via its mean-variance mixture structure. Conditioning on the GIG mixing variable reduces the problem to Gaussian moment calculations and known GIG power moments, avoiding direct integration with Bessel functions. The variance gamma (VG), normal inverse Gaussian (NIG), hyperbolic, Normal, and Student t distributions emerge as natural special or limiting cases of the generalized hyperbolic family. This approach offers a substantially simpler and more transparent derivation, facilitating both implementation and verification.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Multimodal Data Mixtures
papers.abstract: Frontier AI systems are increasingly natively multimodal, jointly pretrained on multiple modalities, such as text, vision, and audio. However, the scientific understanding of the multimodal data mixtures used to pretrain these systems --- how much of each modality to mix, and at what potential interference cost to the others --- is largely absent or gatekept. In this work, we derive data mixing scaling laws for three modalities: text, vision, and audio. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly adopt Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, as MoEs scale efficiently and partially limit cross-modal interference. We therefore use MoEs to conduct 268 experiments ranging from 457M to 8.3B parameters, on up to 150 billion tokens. Our work leads to multiple actionable insights into multimodal data mixing for training MLLMs. First, compute optima are modality-specific: audio modality is model-heavy, favoring scaling parameters over tokens, while text and vision require balanced scaling of model size and data. Second, repeating vision or audio data beyond 2x yields negligible benefits. Finally, cross-modal interactions are highly asymmetric: vision strongly interferes with audio, whereas audio's interference with learning text and vision is negligible. Overall, we provide a principled foundation for understanding the multimodal data mixtures needed to train frontier MLLMs.

papers.title: Exponential Quantum Advantage in Stationary Signal Sensing
papers.abstract: Sensing time-varying signals is essential for precision measurement and for characterizing fluctuations in physical systems. In this work, we show that quantum entanglement provides an exponential advantage in the acquisition time required to learn the temporal statistics of a stationary classical signal. The task is to estimate the characteristic function of joint displacements on selected bosonic modes within a fixed-duration window, using continuous measurements of one signal realization. We present an entanglement-assisted scheme based on two-mode squeezed probes and local Bell measurements with protected idlers, and bound its acquisition time accounting for readout noise and correlations between signal windows. For a strictly stationary pulse family, it achieves polynomial acquisition time at inverse-polynomial accuracy with logarithmic squeezing and polynomial photon number. On the other hand, we prove that any local idler-free protocols require acquisition time exponential in the number of selected temporal modes per window. This lower bound holds for both sequentially prepared and arbitrarily temporally entangled probes, allowing non-Gaussian inputs and measurements and causal classical feedback, as long as each output is measured destructively within its time bin. These results establish an exponential quantum learning advantage for a single continuously monitored stationary signal, with the sensing cost measured by total acquisition time.

papers.title: Hyperpolarization-enabled cooperative molecular magnetic amplification
papers.abstract: Detecting weak magnetic fields at hertz frequencies is central to biomagnetism, geophysical sensing, and searches for new physics, yet it remains challenging because of technical systematics and environmental noise. Here, we realize a continuously operating molecular magnetic amplifier. Signal amplification by reversible exchange (SABRE) parahydrogen-based hyperpolarization maintains non-equilibrium spin order at zero field, turning scalar-coupled nuclear spins in liquid state molecules into an active, frequency-selective gain medium. Measurements of its complex magnetic susceptibility ($χ$) reveal an intrinsic response of $ | χ| \approx$ 10. By feeding the collectively generated magnetic field back to the spins below the threshold for self-sustained $J$-oscillation, we extend the effective spin coherence and cooperatively enhance the susceptibility up to $ | χ| \approx$ 80. Near threshold, this produces approximately fourfold amplification of a weak (20 pT) magnetic field at 3.37 Hz at the sensor location. These results establish hyperpolarized molecules as a tunable active magnetic medium for narrowband quantum sensing and precision measurement.

papers.title: Transport kinetics in excitonic Mott insulator
papers.abstract: Indirect excitons (IXs) in a periodic moiré potential in a van der Waals heterostructure form an experimental platform for exploring Bose-Hubbard physics, including the superfluid state and the Mott insulator state. The realization of these collective states requires low-disorder materials. In particular, the localization due to the Mott insulator must be distinguished from disorder-induced localization. We studied the transport kinetics of IXs in a MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ van der Waals heterostructure with an anomalously high IX mobility, consistent with superfluidity. This high-mobility transport demonstrates that disorder-induced localization is negligible. We found a remarkable suppression of this efficient IX transport, directly indicating the Mott insulator. As the IX density increases during the excitation pulse, the IX cloud initially expands and then contracts upon entering the Mott insulator phase. The emergence of IX cloud contraction is accompanied by a peak in the IX spatial distribution at the origin. Our simulations reproduce the observed non-monotonic IX transport kinetics, including the temporal expansion and contraction of the IX cloud, as well as the peak in its spatial distribution.

papers.title: ByteMark: A Unified Byte-Level Watermark for Detection Across Language Models
papers.abstract: As watermarking of LLM-generated text enters deployment, users increasingly need to check text whose source is unknown. Existing detectors read the watermark through a specific tokenizer or embedding pipeline, and even if all providers adopted the same watermarking method, differences in these representations would leave their watermarks incompatible, and the text alone does not reveal which representation produced it. We propose ByteMark, a unified watermarking scheme that defines its signal on the UTF-8 bytes of published text. Models with different tokenizers embed this signal under one public specification and key, and a single detector verifies the text from the text and key alone. When the tokenizer or embedding model of a baseline detector is replaced, its detection degrades sharply, whereas ByteMark, which uses neither, retains its detection rate; ByteMark also remains detectable when participating models continue or rewrite the text.

papers.title: Frustratingly Easy Agentic RAG via Portable Skills: A Case Study in Customer Support
papers.abstract: Enterprise workflow automation typically requires retrieving a complete and accurate set of relevant information from large operational document corpora (SOPs, policy documents) given a specific scenario or request. In customer support (CS), for example, human specialists must determine the correct sequence of resolution steps for each case, a task that demands precise grounding in policy documentation. Meeting this bar in production typically requires complex document chunking, indexing, and retrieval pipelines, often layered with learned re-rankers, query rewriters, and bespoke agentic RAG infrastructure. We report a deployment case study of a simpler alternative: a portable skill consisting of a natural-language instruction, lightweight tools (a retrieval API, format-checking scripts), and a corpus enriched with an LLM-generated navigation layer, which is a structured "Wikipedia-style" index over the underlying documents. This agentic RAG approach is straightforward to implement (1-2 engineer days), portable across capable agentic harnesses (e.g., Claude Code), and performs strongly on the challenging task of CS resolution workflow generation, achieving 99.2% procedural equivalence to human-approved ground truth and 83.3% evidence sufficiency. It is also roughly an order of magnitude slower per case than our deployed production assistant (~90 s vs. ~8-9 s), so we claim no latency advantage. Our claim is scoped to that setting: a mature, well-curated corpus, a latency-tolerant workflow, and human review of every case. There, the skill did the work of a complex RAG stack, and maintenance became a matter of editing text and data rather than retraining models.

papers.title: Large Out-of-plane Polarization in Two-dimensional Bi2O3 Monolayers Predicted by an AI-driven Inverse-design Workflow
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) polar oxides with built-in electric fields offer promising opportunities for nanoscale electronics, optoelectronics, and surface charge engineering. However, their discovery remains challenging due to the enormous structural complexity of nonlayered oxide networks. Here, we combine inverse structural design with a machine-learning interatomic potential and first-principles calculations to explore 2D oxide configurations. Using Bi2O3 as a representative system, we identify two previously unreported polar monolayers with tetragonal and orthorhombic symmetries. Both structures exhibit vertically separated Bi and O sublayers, giving rise to pronounced intrinsic polarity with Berry-phase 2D polarizations of 34.12 and 37.15 pC/m, respectively. Notably, the o-Bi2O3 monolayer exhibits one of the largest reported out-of-plane polarizations among 2D oxides. Both monolayers exhibit dynamical stability, finite-temperature structural integrity, and wide band gaps (~3.8 eV). The large polarization originates from dimensionality-induced reconstruction of the nonlayered Bi-O network, which breaks local coordination symmetry and produces out-of-plane charge redistribution, while the stereochemically active Bi 6s2 lone pair further favors asymmetric Bi-O bonding. These findings suggest dimensionality-induced local-coordination symmetry breaking as a promising design motif for high-polarization 2D oxides, and demonstrate the utility of combining inverse design with machine-learning-assisted screening to explore unconventional polar phases in nonlayered oxide networks.

papers.title: Characteristic Modes of Non-minimally Coupled Thick Branes
papers.abstract: Characteristic modes provide important information about the intrinsic properties and dynamical response of gravitational systems. In this work, we investigate characteristic modes of thick branes with a non-minimally coupled bulk scalar field. Two representative thick brane solutions are considered, corresponding to a single-kink scalar configuration and a deformed kink configuration with internal structure, respectively. By analyzing the tensor perturbation equations, we first examine the localization of the graviton zero mode in the two brane models. For both brane models, the graviton zero mode is localized on the brane. No pronounced resonant Kaluza--Klein (KK) modes are found for the single-kink brane at $ξ=1/7$. For the deformed brane, we investigate the resonant KK modes at $ξ=0.99$, finding that increasing the deformation parameter $k$ leads to more resonant modes and a longer-lived first resonance. We then calculate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of both brane models independently in the frequency and time domains. The quasinormal frequencies (QNFs) obtained by the independent methods agree well for the low overtones. The masses and decay rates of the resonant KK modes agree closely with the real parts and the magnitudes of the imaginary parts of the corresponding QNFs, respectively.

papers.title: MemForm: Benchmarking Memory Formation Poisoning in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Long-term memory enables LLM agents to learn from past interactions but exposes memory formation to adversarial influence. Existing studies primarily organize memory poisoning by attack channels, corruption patterns, or lifecycle stages, leaving formation interfaces insufficiently characterized. We formulate Memory Formation Poisoning as adversarial manipulation of the interfaces through which persistent agent memory is produced and committed, and introduce MemForm, a controlled diagnostic benchmark covering five interfaces: Content, Evidence, Scope, Selection, and Path Poisoning. We introduce Selection and Path Poisoning as controlled intervention categories that isolate retention and consolidation order effects, respectively. Each category pairs clean and poisoned conditions with interface-specific controls. Evaluations across six LLMs and two response formats reveal broad susceptibility at all five interfaces under the evaluated memory protocols and implementations. Crucially, authentic experiences with successful outcomes do not guarantee reliable behavior after memory formation: changes to contextual support, retention, or consolidation order can induce undesirable downstream behavior. In particular, consolidation order can alter behavior even with identical retained experiences, depending on the memory formation procedure. Additional analyses show that interface applicability depends on memory architecture and that Path Poisoning susceptibility depends on the updater. The evaluated defenses provide incomplete mitigation that varies by interface. These findings motivate protecting both what is committed to persistent memory and how memory is formed from experiences. Code and data are available at https://github.com/opanhw/memform-code.

papers.title: Minimax Wasserstein Testing under Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: We study Wasserstein-$p$ goodness-of-fit and two-sample testing under differential privacy. For general compact metric spaces, we establish upper and lower bounds on the minimax separation radii in terms of covering numbers, matching up to logarithmic factors. On the hypercube $[0,1]^d$, these bounds match up to constant factors for two-sample testing in all dimensions and for goodness-of-fit testing whenever $d\neq 4p$, thereby closing logarithmic gaps in existing non-private results. At the critical case $(d,p)=(4,1)$, we further show that a logarithmic factor is unavoidable by establishing matching minimax bounds for non-private Wasserstein-$1$ goodness-of-fit testing under a bounded-density assumption. Finally, for unbounded domains, we establish minimax-optimal separation rates up to logarithmic factors under an exponential tail condition.

papers.title: Fluctuation-based evaluation of thermal conductivity using deviational phonon Monte Carlo simulations
papers.abstract: We develop a fluctuation based Monte Carlo method for evaluating thermal conductivity within the phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) framework. Starting from the energy based variance reduced formulation of the BTE, we derive a relation between the spatial spreading of deviational phonon energy and the macroscopic heat conduction equation. The resulting formulation expresses thermal conductivity in terms of the mean square displacement of deviational phonon particles, without imposing thermal reservoirs. Consequently, thermal conductivity along multiple directions can be evaluated from a single simulation. The method is demonstrated for crystalline silicon at room temperature in bulk, square nanowires, and anisotropic polycrystalline nanostructures. The calculated thermal conductivities agree with theoretical predictions, including the size dependence induced by phonon boundary scattering and the mode-resolved contributions. For anisotropic polycrystalline structures, the method simultaneously resolves the directional thermal conductivities and captures their dependence on grain morphology. These results demonstrate the validity of the proposed fluctuation-based approach for evaluating thermal conductivity across different transport regimes and structural configurations.

papers.title: Products of co-sober spaces need not be co-sober
papers.abstract: We answer negatively the question whether the product of two co-sober spaces must be co-sober. For a nonempty closed subset $A$ of a $T_1$-space $(X,τ)$, we consider the topology consisting of the co-finite open sets together with the $τ$-open sets disjoint from $A$. We determine its $k$-irreducible compact subsets and derive a criterion that produces two compact co-sober spaces whose product contains a non-singleton $k$-irreducible compact saturated subset of the diagonal. Applying the criterion to a specific Kovář--van Douwen space gives two countable compact Fréchet--Urysohn $T_1$ anti-Hausdorff co-sober spaces whose product is not co-sober. A further construction yields a countable compact Fréchet--Urysohn $T_1$ anti-Hausdorff co-sober space whose square is not co-sober. The failure of product closure also gives an alternative proof of the known non-reflectivity of co-sober spaces in the category of $T_0$-spaces.

papers.title: DS and AMDS Symbol-Pair Codes from Three Families of Simple Root Cyclic Codes
papers.abstract: Symbol-pair distances of simple-root cyclic codes are important for evaluating error correction performance under overlapping pair read channels. In this paper, we construct three families of simple-root cyclic codes over finite fields of odd characteristic via generator polynomials. For length \(2q+2\), the minimum symbol-pair distance is \(10\) for every odd prime power \(q\ge 7\), established by excluding invalid support configurations. For length \(4q-4\), when \(q\equiv 3\pmod 4\) and finite field constraints hold, it is \(9\) or \(10\). For length \(2(q-1)\), reciprocal-polynomial analysis shows it is \(11\) or \(12\). All obtained codes are MDS or AMDS symbol-pair codes.

papers.title: Design Choices for Multimodal Transformer Learning with Missing and Longitudinal Healthcare Data
papers.abstract: Multimodal learning offers the potential to improve predictions by integrating complementary information from heterogeneous data sources. However, multimodal datasets are frequently incomplete, raising important questions about how models should handle missing information. Although recent approaches increasingly rely on Transformer-based architectures for multimodal fusion, incomplete multimodal data introduces challenges such as missing modalities and intra-modal missingness, which motivate key architectural design choices, such as tokenization granularity. In addition, many datasets are longitudinal, with observations collected across multiple time points. The sequential nature of the Transformer architectures provides a natural framework for modeling such data, but introduces additional considerations, such as how temporal information should be represented. In this study, we systematically investigate these design choices using three different cancer datasets. We compare modality-level and feature-level tokenization and evaluate attention masking and imputation as strategies for handling missing information, both naturally occurring in the datasets and synthetically induced. We further investigate approaches for incorporating temporal information in our training process and how to model it. Experiments are conducted with unimodal and multimodal configurations, as well as different levels of missingness for binary survival classification and multiple time encoding strategies for discrete-time survival prediction. Our results show that while multimodal outperforms unimodal results, missing data heavily impacts predictions and thus effective design choices such as tokenization granularity, and intra-missing handling is essential for reliable prediction.

papers.title: From Transfer Probes to Expert Grouping: Evidence from LoRA Post-Training
papers.abstract: A platform that post-trains one base model for many business lines often has more lines than experts it can maintain, so lines must share experts, yet lines seldom come with a taxonomy saying which should share. We ask whether transfer probes (train on one source, measure paired changes on all sources) can discover a grouping when the standard one is unknown. To test probes against a reference, we use seven public sources that do have a label tree (five mathematics subfields and two kinds of programming, standing in for business lines) and treat the tree's grouping as a label reference that the evaluator holds and the method does not. With four LoRA experts under fixed per-source exposure and per-expert budgets, we compare a purely probe-derived grouping and an uninformed uniform default (whose tied routing serves every line from one expert) against this reference. Trained once for one interval from a shared warm-up state and routed by a rule fixed by each allocation, neither reached the prespecified practical gain of 2 percentage points, and both had lower overall utility than the reference ($-2.43$ and $-2.54$ pp; 95\% intervals below zero). In a post hoc comparison, the probe-derived grouping was indistinguishable from the uniform default ($+0.11$ pp, $[-1.25,+1.54]$). In fixed-budget LoRA post-training, a grouping built from initial-state single-source probes thus did not deliver the advantage predicted from the probes once carried to a later training state, a finite budget, and specified routing.

papers.title: Neither True nor False: Do LLMs Represent Truth-Value Gaps in Plural Predication?
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to summarize and verify claims in critical sources that inform consequential decisions. Such claims are full of plural definites. If three of five patients improved after taking drug A, the claim the patients improved after drug A is not true, since two did not, yet its negation, the patients didn't improve after drug A, is not true either, since three did. In formal semantics, this truth-value gap is known as the Homogeneity Gap: both the plural definite and its negation are neither true nor false when the property holds for only a fraction of the plural referent. A model that cannot represent this gap turns mixed evidence into a clean verdict, an error that can be costly in high-stakes use. We introduce HomogeneityNLI, a diagnostic dataset of 1,000 minimal pair items crossing determiner, polarity, and group composition across ten logical conditions. Evaluating seven open-weight models, we uncover a pervasive Bivalence Bias: models assign plural definites their homogeneous truth conditions. In the zero-shot setting, no model recognizes the gap for both polarities in more than 15% of scenarios, and negated definites are judged False in 84% of cases. Explicit linguistic rules, chain-of-thought, and enumeration prompts produce unstable, model-specific effects that often entrench the bias. Our findings indicate that current open-weight LLMs acquire the truth conditions of plural predication but not its trivalent logic, and cannot yet be trusted to summarize or verify claims whose evidence is mixed.

papers.title: SceneForesee: Learning Scene Evolution for Spatiotemporal Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large multimodal models (LMMs) need to understand how entities move and interact as a scene develops. This requires following the same entities over time and relating their observed motion to subsequent changes. We formulate Scene Evolution Understanding (SEU), a task for predicting and interpreting this change. Given observed video, a model estimates entity histories and predicts one scene continuation through future trajectories and Events, accompanied by Visual Evidence from observed motion and a scene description. We construct SceneForesee, a benchmark for evaluating entity continuity and scene evolution reasoning through paired observed and future scenes with shared entity identities. It contains 144.57K temporal pairs, 1.05M entity correspondences, and 272.49K Events paired with observed evidence. We propose a spatiotemporal reasoning framework, EvoSee, that learns future geometry and Event semantics through shared candidate states and joint assignment. It selects one continuation per entity from observation and uses the selected changes for entity refinement, retention, and scene representation. On SceneForesee, EvoSee outperforms Qwen3.5-9B by 10.45 points in Combined Point-F1 and 17.24 points in Event Global F1. On the 4D reasoning benchmark Dyn-Bench, it improves question answering accuracy and grounding J&F by 4.8 and 3.58 points over their respective base systems. These results support scene evolution as both a prediction target and a dynamic representation that brings predicted entity changes into spatiotemporal reasoning.The project is available at https://github.com/mikubaka88/SceneForesee-Spatiotemporal-Reasoning.

papers.title: Target-ESS Tempered Policy Optimization (TETPO): Smooth Variance Control via Bridge Importance Sampling
papers.abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement-learning post-training of large language models is computationally efficient but inherently off-policy: the learner updates on rollouts generated by a stale policy, while correcting this mismatch requires importance weights that can be extremely heavy-tailed. A small number of trajectories may then dominate an update, collapsing the effective sample size (ESS) and increasing the variance and instability of the resulting gradient estimates. Existing stabilizers apply fixed interventions regardless of the realized severity of weight concentration, either discarding selected samples or reweighting them without adapting the correction strength. We introduce \emph{Target--ESS Tempered Policy Optimization} (TETPO), which replaces each importance weight $ρ$ by $ρ^α$ for a data-adaptive exponent $α\in[0,1]$: $α=1$ preserves the original importance weights, whereas $α=0$ assigns uniform coefficients. For each prompt group, TETPO selects the largest $α$ whose tempered weights satisfy a target ESS fraction $κ$, applying little tempering to healthy groups and stronger tempering when weight degeneracy is severe. At the population level, the tempered coefficients are exact importance weights for a geometric bridge between the sampler and learner policies. The exponent is efficiently found by one-dimensional bisection, while the resulting weights satisfy deterministic bounds on normalized-weight dispersion and weighted-gradient norm that are independent of policy drift, together with a fixed-$α$ bound on bridge-target discrepancy. Power tempering also introduces no explicit zero-weight mask. On mathematical-reasoning benchmarks under high staleness, TETPO outperforms strong on- and off-policy baselines.

papers.title: Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight
papers.abstract: We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category $\mathcal{H}_3$. Its characters are the $γ=0$ Evans--Gannon vector. From $U$ we obtain a diagonal full CFT, and also a holomorphic $E_8$ extension on which $\mathcal{H}_3$ acts by topological defects.

papers.title: Evaluating Semantic Relation Knowledge through Bidirectional Relation Prediction from Gloss Pairs
papers.abstract: Semantic relations organise word senses and are fundamental to lexical semantics. In order to evaluate semantic relation knowledge of large language models (LLMs), we propose a challenging task in which an LLM predicts the relation between two glosses (definitions of senses) presented in two different orders. The predictions for the two orders are evaluated for consistency with the symmetry or asymmetry of semantic relations. Our task is designed for both monolingual and cross-lingual evaluation, allowing us to examine whether relation knowledge remains accessible when the same senses are verbalised through glosses in different languages. We construct a dataset of 3,069 sense pairs, with each sense verbalised in English, Greek, Romanian, Turkish, and Japanese. Experiments with 17 LLMs in zero-shot and five-shot settings reveal generally poor performance. In each setting, only eight LLMs achieve a macro-averaged F1 score significantly above a random baseline, and only one (zero-shot) and two (five-shot) significantly outperform a neural baseline. In particular, LLMs often fail to generate bidirectionally consistent predictions for hypernymy and to make correct predictions for holonymy in either direction. Our results suggest limitations in current LLMs' semantic relation knowledge, both in identifying relations and in respecting asymmetry.

papers.title: Specification-Based Testing of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Model cards, system cards, and safety reports increasingly document LLM safety behaviors, yet safety evaluations typically start from predefined benchmarks rather than asking which documented claims those benchmarks actually test. We introduce LEST (LLM Evaluation through Specification-driven Testing), a framework that treats documented safety claims as specifications for black-box testing. In LEST, each claim determines which benchmark prompt tests it and whether a Refuse-to-Comply transition, where a model refuses a prompt but complies with its mutated version, counts as evidence against it. LEST mutates these prompts to search for counterexamples, manually validates each candidate, and traces validated counterexamples back to the claims they contradict. We evaluate LEST using the system cards of Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 with 97 seed prompts from SORRY-Bench across Mental Health and Self-Harm, Harmful and Violent Content, and Fairness and Bias. Of 56 identified safety claims, 29 (51.8%) are prompt-testable, but only 17 (58.6%) are exercised by an applicable benchmark prompt. Both models refuse >95% of benchmark prompts. Evaluating 1,836 mutated prompts on both models reveals 312 candidate Refuse-to-Comply transitions flagged by automated response classifiers. However, human validation confirms only 19 (6.1%) as both intent-preserving and genuinely compliant, showing automated evaluation substantially overestimates behavioral failures. Tracing these 19 transitions back to the claims reveals counterexamples for 6 of 9 covered claims for which refusal is an applicable oracle. Our results show that benchmark prompts may not be sufficient to validate all documented LLM safety behavior, and automated failure detection requires manual validation. LEST provides end-to-end traceability from natural-language safety documentation to executable tests and human-validated counterexamples.

papers.title: Taylor-Approximation-Based Repair of High Floating-Point Errors
papers.abstract: Numerical libraries can still lose many bits of accuracy on localized ill-conditioned inputs, such as roots, poles, cancellation points, and branch boundaries. This paper presents NPTaylor, a Taylor-approximation-based framework for repairing localized high floating-point errors in numerical C routines. Given a high-error input, a localized repair domain, a high-precision oracle, and an error threshold, NPTaylor searches over Taylor degree, expansion center, segmentation, and floating-point evaluation strategy. It emits guarded C patches that use a generated Taylor evaluator inside the repair domain and fall back to the original routine outside it. Candidate patches are accepted only after validating the emitted C code on recorded local samples, guard endpoints, and the pre-repair peak input. The generated evaluator uses coefficient splitting and compensated Horner evaluation to reduce rounding error introduced by the patch itself. We evaluate NPTaylor on GSL benchmark workloads. On 38 one-input functions, both NPTaylor and AutoRNP repair all 114 configurations across three accuracy thresholds. NPTaylor is 3.33x faster by geometric-mean offline repair time and emits 0.162x as many C bytes. In the strictest setting, its median repair time is 3.74s versus 81.97s for AutoRNP. NPTaylor also repairs localized multi-input benchmark cases beyond AutoRNP's implemented one-input workflow. These results show that Taylor-based guarded patches can provide compact, efficient local repairs, while the claims remain validation-relative rather than full-domain proofs.

papers.title: FreeCHROMA: Generative Chroma Keying from Unaligned Background References
papers.abstract: In film production, chroma keying composites an approved foreground performance into a new environment, but conventional workflows require coordinated background plates and dedicated harmonization. Recent generative methods often require pre-aligned backgrounds, focus on background-conditioned foreground relighting, or represent the environment only through an edited first frame. These restrictions limit background selection, scene composition, and camera motion while adding preparation or editing effort. We present FreeCHROMA, which adapts a pretrained video diffusion model in a parameter-efficient manner for generative video compositing from one to three unaligned background references. The model integrates the foreground into the referenced environment, preserving foreground identity, motion, and fine visual details while generating a spatiotemporally coherent background. Foreground-background harmonization occurs within the same generation process, without a separate relighting stage. Optional text instructions help disambiguate complex spatial relationships and camera behavior. To train the model, we construct pseudo-paired data from readily available real monocular videos through foreground-background separation and augmentation with existing foundation models. The original videos serve as training targets, while automated processing and quality verification enable scalable data construction. Across reference fidelity, foreground preservation, scene integration, harmonization, and overall video quality, FreeCHROMA consistently outperforms recent compositing and conditional video-generation baselines, with particularly clear gains under camera motion. FreeCHROMA relaxes the constraints of existing tools to enable end-to-end generative chroma keying from unaligned inputs, with exploratory experiments demonstrating its potential in robotics.

papers.title: Compact localization and co-sobriety of Smyth power spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a compact-localization theorem for finite iterates of the Smyth power space. Successive union maps assign to every finite-level Smyth object a canonical least compact saturated carrier in the original space, and co-sobriety at each positive finite level is equivalent to co-sobriety of the corresponding iterates over all compact saturated carriers. Consequently, if every compact saturated subspace of a $T_0$-space $X$ is stably compact---in particular, if every such subspace is Hausdorff---then $\PS^n(X)$ is co-sober for every finite $n\geq 1$. This applies to every $k_1$-Hausdorff space and hence to every Hausdorff or metrizable space. For the first iterate, we also give a direct full-Vietoris argument, independent of stable compactness, which shows that each $k$-irreducible compact saturated family is generated by its union.

papers.title: Symmetric two-level preconditioning for the method of reflections
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze a symmetric two-level preconditioner for the method of reflections for Laplace problems in perforated domains. Using constant boundary modes, we define a coarse correction through a symmetric coercive dual formulation. Combining this coarse correction with parallel reflection corrections gives a symmetric positive definite preconditioner for solving the dual system by the conjugate gradient method. Under a geometric separation condition, we prove a condition number bound independent of the number and sizes of the holes and the diameter of the ambient domain. We also derive geometry-dependent convergence estimates for the one-level methods that explain the need for a coarse correction.

papers.title: KV4-RL: Unlocking Faster Asynchronous Rollouts for RLVR with INT4 KV Cache Quantization
papers.abstract: Asynchronous rollout improves the efficiency of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) by reducing under-utilization during long-tail generation. Sustained concurrency also concentrates context processing into fewer decode steps, increasing the KV workload per step. We characterize this \emph{KV concentration} and find that KV cache quantization delivers substantially greater acceleration than weight-only and weight-activation quantization in our matched-workload comparisons. However, INT4 KV rollout can degrade learning even with token-level truncated importance sampling (TIS). We propose \emph{KV4-RL}, which combines calibration-free INT4 KV quantization with selective INT8 protection of attention sinks and recent context. Protecting a bounded number of positions reduces sampler mismatch while retaining most of the speedup from INT4. Across 400 iterations of Qwen3-8B-Base GRPO training, KV4-RL achieves $1.80\times$ cumulative rollout speedup and $1.27\times$ cumulative full-iteration speedup over BF16 rollout, reaching $1.97\times$ rollout speedup over the final 50 iterations. Under a common BF16 evaluator, its final six-benchmark mean accuracy is within 0.5 percentage points of BF16-rollout training for both Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base.

papers.title: Jevolution: A Framework for Studying Communication and Collective Dynamics in AI Agents
papers.abstract: Experiments with remote decision-making agents depend on more than the policy: the world may change during inference, the simulator determines which actions are available, and births and immigration alter who can act. We present Jevolution, an instrumented spatial predator-prey framework that makes these dependencies explicit. Its reference implementation separates the evolving world, asynchronous request scheduling, controller adapters, and experiment records. The model combines local observations, energy and resource constraints, predefined signals, and inherited scalar traits. We describe these mechanisms using the ODD protocol and distinguish implemented controls from research questions requiring additional interventions. Free synthetic fixtures exercise scheduling, signaling, and inheritance against the pinned implementation; they validate specified software behavior rather than model intelligence or ecological realism. A completed communication case study illustrates the end-to-end workflow using Jev to control both species. Across 6 complete habitat-seed pairs, the mean signals-on minus signals-off difference in normalized rabbit abundance was -0.0095 (nominal 95% pair-bootstrap interval [-0.0772, 0.0602]). This small study does not resolve the direction of the signal-system effect. The contribution is an inspectable experimental system and its evidence boundaries, not a new policy-learning algorithm or a demonstration of emergent language, adaptive selection, or biological predictive validity.

papers.title: On the generalization of Christol's theorem to domains of finite type over finite fields
papers.abstract: We generalize Christol's theorem---which characterizes algebraic power series over a finite field in terms of automatic coefficient sequences---to completions of domains of finite type over a finite field~$\mathbb{F}_{q}$. Let $A$ be such a domain of dimension~$d$ and $\mathfrak{a}$ an ideal of depth~$d$. In the $\mathfrak{a}$-adic completion $\hat{A}$, choose an $\hat{A}$-regular sequence $\boldsymbol{x}=\{x_{1},\dots,x_{d}\}\subset\hat{\mathfrak{a}}$ and a set of representatives $E$ of $\hat{A}/(\boldsymbol{x})$ that is an $\mathbb{F}_{q}$-vector subspace consisting of algebraic elements. Every element $y\in\hat{A}$ then admits a unique expansion $y=\sum_{u\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}a_{u}x^{u}$ with coefficients $a_{u}\in E$. We prove that $y$ is algebraic over $A$ if and only if the coefficient sequence $\{a_{u}\}_{u\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}$ is $q$-automatic. The proof relies on a careful study of henselizations, which are shown to coincide with the algebraic closures inside the completions under certain conditions. As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of the automaticity of $β$-expansions for formal Laurent series over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$, answering questions posed by Hbaib--Mkaouar and Scheicher--Sirvent.

papers.title: Quadrature-detected zero-to-ultralow-field nuclear magnetic resonance
papers.abstract: We present the concept of quadrature-detected zero-to-ultralow-field nuclear magnetic resonance (QD ZULF NMR). Two orthogonal sensors, atomic optically pumped magnetometers, are used to separately detect components of oscillating sample magnetization, which are then combined into a quadrature signal. This approach enables the distinction of positive and negative resonance frequencies with respect to the laboratory frame---such that absolute signs of gyromagnetic ratios can be determined. In addition, QD ZULF NMR reduces peak density and overlap compared to ZULF NMR with single-axis detection, while providing richer information about nuclear-spin dynamics. As an illustration, we present experimental $J$-spectra for thermally polarized [$^{13}$C]-formic acid and [$^{13}$C]-methanol, compounds commonly used in ZULF NMR which represent XA and XA$_3$ spin systems, respectively. A theoretical framework describing QD ZULF NMR signals is provided.

papers.title: Signed Quantities and Quadrilaterals: Geometry without Cases
papers.abstract: Ordinary angles and unsigned areas discard orientation, and much of the case analysis in plane geometry is the price of that loss. Signed quantities (directed angles, oriented areas and directed distances) keep the signs and so let one argument serve for every configuration. We illustrate this with results that hold uniformly for convex, concave and crossed quadrilaterals: the diagonal area formula, an identity expressing one diagonal in terms of the sides and the other diagonal, a test for a pair of parallel sides, a theorem on equidiagonal quadrilaterals (such a quadrilateral has a pair of equal opposite sides if and only if it has a pair of parallel opposite sides), and a single ratio of directed distances that decides whether the vertices lie on an ellipse, only on hyperbolas, or on a circle.

papers.title: SecReason: Vulnerability Detection and In-Stream Self-Repair for LLM Code Generation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) may introduce security vulnerabilities into generated code, which can persist into production when verification focuses on functional correctness. Existing defenses act before, during, or after generation, but none inspects the code during generation. Security prompts and retrieved security knowledge act before any code exists, constrained decoding limits token choices but cannot guide repair, and post-hoc repair must regenerate the full response. Reasoning LLMs draft code early in their streamed chain of thought, and in this pre-delivery window the code exists only inside the reasoning stream. We present SecReason, an in-stream defense that monitors this window. Dual-track incremental scanning applies security rules, checking each statement as it is emitted and tracing dataflows across the accumulated code. When a security rule fires, SecReason interrupts generation, inserts an in-stream warning, and resumes decoding, so the model repairs the draft within the same reasoning trace without regenerating the full response. On tasks where unassisted generation introduces vulnerabilities, \system raises the share of runs delivering secure and functionally correct code from below 15\% to 72.8\%--98.1\% on \tool{CWEval} and \tool{SecCodeBench}. \system consumes fewer tokens than post-hoc repair, and when security rules misfire on secure code, it limits the functional regressions from false warnings.

papers.title: Quantum-Fisher-information-aware optimization yields a quantum reservoir advantage over tuned classical reservoirs
papers.abstract: We show that a quantum reservoir computer optimized with its quantum Fisher information (QFI) has a quantum advantage over a classical reservoir of equal readout cost, provided by a quantum-information advantage: optimizing the quantum parameters with the QFI metric. On Mackey-Glass forecasting, a driven Jaynes-Cummings reservoir with one to three atoms beats a tuned echo-state network at every size from 4 to 30 trained weights, by 25-69% in held-out error, and is ahead of 99.5% of 10,000 random networks. After grid and Bayesian searches saturate, the QFI-aware stage lowers the error by 29-51% at 12-30 weights, beyond equal-budget black-box search or classical-parameter gradients alone, and at 30 weights turns a loss into a win. We then derive a fundamental QFI bound on the first-order rate of change of the retrained loss and factorize the gap to this bound into five link efficiencies that identify the physical mechanism limiting optimization.

papers.title: Global existence and convergence of a density heat flow for strictly subcritical Liouville systems
papers.abstract: We study a density heat flow associated with normalized Liouville systems on a closed connected Riemannian surface, and we show that this flow leads to the existence of solutions for the corresponding subcritical Liouville systems. The coupling matrix is symmetric and entrywise nonnegative, with no invertibility, irreducibility or inverse-matrix sign assumption. Under the strict subcriticality conditions $8π\sum_{i\in J}ρ_i>\sum_{i,j\in J}a_{ij}ρ_iρ_j$ for every nonempty set of components $J$, every smooth positive initial density of masses $ρ_i>0$ generates a unique global smooth positive solution converging in every $C^m$ norm to a stationary density. The limiting potentials solve the stationary Liouville system. Our proof uses entropy coercivity and a gradient inequality in the density variables, which also yields algebraic or exponential convergence rates.

papers.title: Learning to Extrapolate in Depth with Looped Transformers
papers.abstract: Looped transformers reuse a single block across iterations, raising a natural question: how far can a block trained at one depth be safely extrapolated to greater depths? We study this question for all-pairs graph connectivity, where harder graphs require longer-range information propagation. We show that under exchangeability and symmetric positive initialization, population training at depth K converges to an update rule governed by a single effective parameter that balances graph propagation against fitting structure unresolved at training depth. This trade-off creates a finite extrapolation window: too few test-time loops provide insufficient propagation, while too many eventually create false connections. We derive explicit endpoints for this window and bound the graph hardness solvable beyond training as a function of training depth and hardness. In particular, a test depth chosen solely from the training distribution can guarantee recovery on substantially harder graphs, with a certified depth gain that grows exponentially as training depth outpaces training hardness. Experiments validate the predicted windows and show how compute budget and initialization affect the optimal training depth.

papers.title: Convergence of Least Squares Methods for PDEs on R^d with Shallow ReLU^k Networks
papers.abstract: We establish inverse inequalities in Gaussian Sobolev norms for shallow $\mathrm{ReLU}^k$ trial spaces. The estimates identify the sharp regularity threshold and quantify the dependence on parameter separation and bias magnitude. Based on these estimates, we prove convergence of weighted least squares discretizations of linear PDEs on $\mathbb R^d$ using shallow networks with prescribed inner parameters and finitely many residual samples in an expanding ball. Under suitable stability and regularity assumptions, we obtain an error bound of order $h^{k+(d+1)/2-r}δ_\pm^{-(S-r)}$ in the Gaussian Sobolev norm of order $S$, up to logarithmic factors, where $r$ is the PDE order, $h$ is the parameter fill distance, and $δ_\pm$ is the antipodal separation. The convergence results cover deterministic and random sampling and extend to fixed bounded regions by restriction. We construct parameter sets with $δ_\pm\asymp h$, yielding a convergence rate in terms of the network width that matches a lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results and provide practical guidance on balancing accuracy and stability.

papers.title: The strong Ramanujan bound for Drinfeld modular forms
papers.abstract: The Ramanujan bound states that the degree of the trace of the $\mathfrak{p}$-Hecke operator on a space of weight $k$ Drinfeld cusp forms is at most $d(k-2)/2$, where $\mathfrak{p}$ is a prime of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$. We prove the strong Ramanujan bound, which states that at level 1, this bound can be improved to $d(k-(q+1))/2$. In addition, we classify when the strong Ramanujan bound is sharp; surprisingly, this turns out to depend on $\mathfrak{p}$ only through the parity of its degree. We also prove results related to the smallest slope of the Atkin operator and mod $p$ distributions of Frobenius polynomials of Drinfeld modules over finite fields.

papers.title: Sharp Constants and Extremizers in Homogeneous Tree BMO
papers.abstract: We develop a finite-tree formalism for sharp inequalities on real-valued, mean-centered $\operatorname{L}^1$-BMO over homogeneous $q$-ary filtrations. A reduction theorem identifies local and global sharp constants with the supremum of finite-depth constants. Finite anchoring gives compact optimization problems and rational extremizers under rational piecewise-linear hypotheses, while stable centering shows that imposing zero root average preserves the supremum over all depths. The principal application is the absolute-value map: we construct centered examples in which taking absolute values increases the BMO seminorm and obtain bounds strictly below the universal factor $2$. Jensen-defect Carleson functionals and martingale-difference envelopes provide further applications, illustrating distinct anchoring mechanisms and the differences between finite-depth rationality, stabilization, and global attainment.

papers.title: Re-executing Coding-Agent Evaluations: Unchanged Decisions and Unresolved Policy Risk
papers.abstract: Executable tests grade large language model (LLM) coding-agent patches for leaderboards, rewards and self-improvement. Two preregistered re-execution studies returned negative results. SWE-bench Pro v1's offline option rejected none of 59 accepted Go patches whose grading configuration changed. Their exploratory, unweighted upper confidence limit is 4.95% under candidate independence, leaving a 3% exposed-patch risk unresolved; the preregistered estimator uses inverse sampling-probability weights. An extension was inconclusive. In a selected stratum, a reconstructed module cache built from the reference solution's dependencies rejected accepted alternatives from four models that passed with their own dependencies. Re-executing 1,929 selected agent-version/task evaluations from the Darwin Gödel Machine's archive preserved best-agent selection and system-variant ranking, with search history and scores of evaluations not rerun fixed. Exploratory host, image and adapted-grader comparisons also preserved them. Seven of 23 disagreements with archived verdicts did not recur on a second host; rebuilt images changed 16 three-run majority verdicts (0.83%) under four-CPU execution. We provide an evidence-to-claim summary, lessons for grader audits and an anonymous replication package. These results concern accepted patches and fixed-history decisions; general policy safety and adaptive-learning robustness require broader evaluations.

papers.title: PINNs for N=2* holography
papers.abstract: Can a holographic theory be reconstructed from its equation of state? We investigate this question using physics-informed neural networks in the bosonic-mass sector of the Pilch--Warner model. We first validate the PINN approach against an analytic solution encoding the leading high-temperature corrections to the conformal equation of state. We then reconstruct nonlinear black-brane geometries and the scalar potential using thermodynamics, ultraviolet asymptotics, Ward identities, and horizon regularity. Independent solutions of the bulk Einstein-scalar equations demonstrate that accurately reproducing thermodynamics with a trained PINN does not guarantee an accurate reconstruction of the scalar potential. High-precision knowledge of the high-temperature equation of state constrains nonlinear interactions in the bulk scalar potential. Fixing the cubic coupling to its exact PW value, motivated by this high-temperature extraction, reduces the maximum sampled error in the reconstructed scalar self-interactions by a factor of $\sim 15$ compared with constraining only the bulk scalar mass. Adding knowledge of the bulk viscosity of the gauge theory plasma further reduces this error by an additional factor of $\sim 13$, with independent forward solutions reproducing the bulk viscosity within $0.09\%$.

papers.title: Rethinking SZZ Search Strategies: Lessons from Claude Code
papers.abstract: Identifying bug-inducing commits (BICs) is important for studying software bugs and maintaining software, yet the accuracy of existing SZZ methods remains limited. Although various improvements have been proposed, many SZZ methods still rely on code tracing, which searches for BICs by tracing code changed in a bug-fixing commit (BFC) back to earlier commits. However, this approach may miss the actual BIC when the code responsible for introducing a bug differs from the code modified to fix it. To overcome this limitation, we investigate whether BIC identification can be improved by exploring search strategies that are not constrained to start with code tracing. We use Claude Code, a coding agent that has demonstrated high BIC identification accuracy in prior research, to explore such strategies. Rather than prescribing a search process or providing predefined candidate commits, we allow Claude Code to independently investigate a Git repository. We evaluate its identification accuracy and search behavior on 79 Java cases from 70 repositories. In 79.7% of runs, Claude Code reviewed commit histories before inspecting individual code diffs. It used commit messages to select changes for closer inspection. With this approach, Claude Code achieves an F1 score of 0.771, significantly outperforming all ten evaluated SZZ baselines. Our failure analysis also reveals incorrect oracle labels and ambiguities in BIC definitions in the studied evaluation dataset. After reconstructing the evaluation dataset to address these issues, Claude Code achieves an F1 score of 0.938. A key lesson from Claude Code for improving SZZ search strategies is to use semantic information to find relevant commits and then examine their code changes, rather than starting with code tracing.

papers.title: Soft-to-Rigid: Shape Continuation as an Alternative Search for Packing Congruent Shapes
papers.abstract: Searches for dense packings of congruent shapes move rigid pieces. Hardening starts each piece as its inscribed disk and deforms it into the target shape while the container is compressed. We ask whether it is a search worth running alongside existing ones, and test it at matched budget and comparable tuning against rigid starts, growth, simulated annealing and perturbation--compression on seven families of squares, triangles, hexagons and disks in squares, triangles and circles (188 instances), scoring each method by the lowest container size it reaches. Hardening is not a better default: tuned rigid starts reach the lowest size most often. It is a different search. On squares in a square it reaches packings the other four methods miss, including Trump's n = 11 and Wainwright's n = 19 in 32 runs per method, and in a targeted follow-up campaign at ten times the budget (16 runs per method) it is the only one to reach the best known packings for n = 17 and n = 26, while annealing alone reaches n = 27. In exploratory ablations, compressing disks and then switching to polygons at once, or growing rigid polygons along hardening's area schedule, shows no detectable difference from rigid starts, and hardening's unique packings contain more tilted pieces. The bias costs elsewhere: hardening is worse on triangles and on four families held out from all development, where the short-pilot policy we tested showed no detected advantage over always starting rigid. Shape continuation is an alternative search that reaches different packings, worth keeping beside rigid ones; we did not show that splitting a fixed budget between them pays, and we have no test that predicts where it helps. Search campaigns were planned before they ran, with amendments, exploratory analyses and post-hoc checks identified separately; every run is replayable and every number is generated from an event log.

papers.title: Evaluating Bias in Chinese Large Language Models across Tasks and Registers: Task Operationalization Effects and Irony Classification Risks
papers.abstract: In Chinese content governance, large language models are increasingly used to identify toxic and discriminatory expressions, yet both task operationalization and ironic expression can alter bias measurement readings. We conducted a preregistered multi-task behavioral audit of multiple Chinese large language models. In the content classification experiment, the core panel's classification error rate rose from 10.9% in the formal register to 23.5% in the yinyang (an echoic-irony register) version, a risk difference of +12.7 percentage points. (95% CI [+9.7, +15.7]). Inter-rater agreement was lower in the yinyang register (majority-vote kappa = 0.299), so the increase contains a component of label uncertainty propagation, but the direction of increase was consistent under both adjudicated and majority-vote reference standards. Explicit irony-aware prompts reduced the intervention panel's error rate by 9.6 percentage points.
