For prediction, we introduce EPT-X, a neural point process that adds a history-dependent mixture-of-Erlang renewal channel to a linear Hawkes backbone. Its intensity and compensator remain in closed form, its states follow an affine recursion that trains with a parallel scan, and it can start from the certified fit of the measurement model. EPT-X has the best test likelihood on all five LOBSTER order-book streams and on Retweet and Taobao, and is level with the best published model on StackOverflow. We also find that the EasyTPP implementation of IntensityFree clamps short inter-event times before scoring, and that the gaps of the EasyTPP Amazon data are uniform on two fixed intervals.

papers.title: TopoMix: Continuous Spatial Mixing for Long-Tailed Data Augmentation
papers.abstract: Most mixing-based augmentation methods improve generalization through a simple idea: combine two training samples with a fixed global ratio or a hard spatial replacement. While effective, this design leaves little room for local variation, which becomes a more visible limitation in long-tailed recognition, where minority classes are especially sensitive to the quality of augmented samples. We propose TopoMix, a training-free augmentation method that replaces fixed mixing with continuous spatial mixing. TopoMix constructs a smooth spatially varying mask from a low-resolution random control grid, bicubic interpolation, and stochastic non-linear shaping, and uses this mask for element-wise image mixing and label reweighting. Without introducing trainable parameters or auxiliary networks, TopoMix offers a simple way to make mixing more flexible in the input space. Experiments on standard long-tailed benchmarks show that it consistently improves over representative mixing-based baselines, indicating that smooth spatial mixing is an effective augmentation strategy for long-tailed recognition.

papers.title: Higher-order semi-rational solutions of the (2+1)-dimensional nonlocal multi-component Yajima--Oikawa system
papers.abstract: Higher-order semi-rational solutions are constructed for the (2+1)-dimensional nonlocal multi-component Yajima-Oikawa system. This system is obtained from its local \(2M\)-component counterpart through a spatial-reflection reduction. Using Hirota's bilinear method and the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili hierarchy reduction, we derive a unified \(6\times6\) block Gram determinant. Its entries involve Schur polynomials and exponential functions. The complex-conjugation and spatial-reflection reductions are imposed through algebraic constraints on the spectral parameters and determinant blocks, with the former ensuring a real-valued denominator tau function. Separate spectral parameter sets are assigned to the rational, breather, and dark-soliton blocks. These solutions describe paired lumps or line rogue waves on breather, dark-soliton, or combined backgrounds. Pure rational, breather, and dark-soliton solutions follow by setting the appropriate block sizes to zero. Asymptotic analysis establishes the elastic interactions of the fundamental breather and dark-soliton pairs and determines their position and phase shifts.

papers.title: Dimensional transition and spectral instability in lattice Hardy inequalities
papers.abstract: Discretization can change a sharp stability threshold even when the continuum threshold is recovered at infinity. We study this phenomenon for the Hardy inequality on the integer lattice in dimensions at least three: its best coefficient agrees with the continuum value through dimension eight and is smaller from dimension nine onwards. We characterize this transition by the total critical defect, the summable error obtained by testing the lattice operator against the critical continuum power. A theta-function representation proves that the defect is negative and strictly decreasing from dimension nine; explicit positive Hardy remainders establish its positivity in dimensions three through eight. An exact energy identity relates this defect to the energy saved by optimizing the profile outside the neighbours of the origin. This exterior remains stable in dimensions eight and nine, locating the first loss of positivity in its coupling to those neighbours. We give self-contained proofs of both dimensional ranges. We then describe how local attraction creates a negative eigenvalue in a general class of lattice operators with critical inverse-square tails. Its magnitude is exponentially small near the threshold, with both the rate and the multiplicative prefactor determined by zero-energy solutions. The result allows connected finite modifications of the lattice and nonradial corrections to the tail. The same analysis controls the spread of the emerging state and gives a two-dimensional return scale for the associated Markov chain in every ambient dimension.

papers.title: FoundationVIO: Enforcing Metric Scale in Feed-forward Visual-Inertial Odometry
papers.abstract: Feed-forward geometric foundation models (GFMs) directly predict dense geometry and camera poses from batches of images. Emerging visual SLAM methods chain together consecutive GFM batches to form dense point cloud maps. A core challenge is how to address the ambiguous geometric scale of GFM predictions: independent predictions are locally consistent up-to-scale but not constrained by any direct physical measurements. Models trained on data with known scale improve the consistency of GFM reconstructions but again do not directly measure it. Consequently, trajectories and 3D reconstructions from GFM-enabled SLAM methods inherit this issue. Motivated by parallels with classical visual-inertial odometry, we introduce FoundationVIO which integrates inertial sensing with GFM predictions to recover metric scale reconstruction using a factor-graph based approach. We demonstrate odometry estimates competitive with classical state-of-the-art VIO methods and accurate dense reconstructions that outperform GFM-enabled SLAM methods. We also add a minimal GFM-based loop-closure mechanism to create a full Visual-Inertial SLAM system capable of creating globally accurate reconstructions and pose estimates. We evaluate our method on three datasets with well known sensor systems and demonstrate its compatibility on ubiquitous camera and IMU sensors. The method runs at approximately real-time on a consumer-grade laptop GPU. Code: https://github.com/ori-drs/FoundationVIO.

papers.title: Do Personalized LLMs Need the Whole Conversation? Matching the Full History with Only 5% of Its Text via Relevance-Filtered Context
papers.abstract: Personalized assistants accumulate long conversation histories, and passing the whole history to an LLM with every request is costly. We show that it is also unnecessary. On PersonaMem-v2 (180 questions), with GPT-5.6-terra and Claude Opus 5.5 as judges, a relevance-filtered context, built by sentence-level retrieval that ranks the history by similarity to the current request and stops at a fixed budget, matches full-history accuracy with only 5% of the text, cutting the judge's input about 20-fold. An LLM summary of the same length performs on par, but it needs an LLM to read the entire history, whereas retrieval needs only a small embedding model. While both sentence-level retrieval and LLM summary perform strongly, retrieval does so while placing the relevant evidence in the context for only 61% of the questions, and an oracle given only that evidence beats the full history by 15.6 points, making better context selection a promising path to surpassing the full history.

papers.title: Counterfactual Rollouts for Offline Contrastive Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Contrastive reinforcement learning (CRL) learns goal-conditioned values by associating state--action pairs with the states subsequently reached, assuming that no unobserved variable jointly affects the recorded action and its outcome. When offline demonstrations come from a demonstrator with information hidden from the learner, this assumption fails and the critic absorbs spurious action--outcome associations. We formalize this setting with confounded Markov decision processes and introduce counterfactual transitions that separate what the data identify from what they do not; minimizing over all compatible transitions yields a worst-case occupancy that lower-bounds the true one. Causal Contrastive Reinforcement Learning (CauCRL) learns a pessimistic counterfactual transition from positive and negative offline demonstrations and trains the critic on counterfactual rollouts, substantially improving success rates over standard CRL on confounded goal-reaching tasks.

papers.title: Partial-coherence weak measurement of polarization qubits with a temporal pointer: theory and experiment
papers.abstract: Weak measurement has proven useful for metrology, for probing quantum paradoxes, and for the direct measurement of quantum states. Weak measurements of polarization qubits with temporal pointers provide a direct route to weak-value characterization, including in regimes where the pointer is only partially coherent. We derive a closed-form expression for the post-selected temporal shift that interpolates between the incoherent and coherent (ideal) weak-measurement limits through a single parameter $ν$, the pointer visibility. The expression is experimentally tested for a range of polarization states spanning three trajectories corresponding to rotations about the principal axes of the Poincaré sphere. Two of the trajectories provide parameter-free benchmarks, with the real part of the weak value following $\cos^2θ$ and $1/2$. In contrast, the weak value along the third trajectory is sensitive to incoherence and is well described by the single-parameter partial-coherence model, from which a reduced pointer visibility is obtained. Time shifts are extracted from the smoothed derivative of the pulse leading edge with internal calibration, reaching few-picosecond precision on 10 ns optical pulses using commercial components. The same apparatus also gives qualitative access to the imaginary quadrature through the frequency centroid, showing that temporal weak measurements remain accessible and quantitative in partially coherent pulsed systems.

papers.title: Transfer Learning for Rhythm Game Chart Generation from Music Transcription and Across Games
papers.abstract: Rhythm games ask the player to act in time with a recording, following a chart: a sequence of actions, each with a time and, depending on the game, a lane, type, or playfield position. Charts are hand-written per recording and difficulty. Automatic generation from audio has been studied with pipeline and end-to-end approaches, and recent work reuses pre-trained audio encoders, but never compares them with one trained from scratch. None of these targets automatic music transcription (AMT), yet most chart times are note onsets, which AMT models locate. We freeze a pre-trained audio encoder, an AMT model in particular, and train only a linear projection and a Transformer decoder on charts. With MuScriptor, this fits human charts more closely than encoders trained from scratch and places more accurate note types than MERT, a music encoder pre-trained without transcription labels. Joint training on three osu! modes raises event F1 on the mode with the fewest charts from 0.492 to 0.506, while charts from Clone Hero, similar in layout, lower it to 0.482. Transfer between games thus appears to depend on charting style and the music covered.

papers.title: MCPDisCo: Seesaw-Mitigated Tuning for MCP-Native Agents
papers.abstract: The Model Context Protocol provides a shared interaction substrate for the agentic web, allowing heterogeneous services to expose capabilities through a standardized interface. Learning to use this ecosystem entails a hierarchy of capabilities: tool-format skills, server-level transfer, and cross-server composition. We present MCPDisCo, an ecosystem-scale reinforcement learning framework for MCP-native agents. Using a Thought-Markov Decision Process (Thought-MDP), the framework explicitly represents internal reasoning alongside routing, execution, and termination and trains on real-server, long-horizon interactions spanning 70 MCP servers and 527 tools across six domains. We study the reasoning--tool seesaw, a joint-learning failure mode in which improvement in one objective can accompany deterioration in the other. To mitigate potential interference, MCPDisCo combines token-masked reward attribution with bidirectional gradient surgery: the former separates direct supervision for reasoning and action spans, while the latter removes conflicting components from both objective gradients in shared parameters. MCPDisCo achieves higher success with fewer chain-of-thought tokens. On the out-of-distribution MCP-Atlas and the GAIA benchmark, MCPDisCo maintains monotone gains, confirming that the learned behavior generalizes beyond the training server distribution and broader agentic tasks. Model weight and implementation are available.

papers.title: CatPortrait: Taming Video Generative Models for Portrait Animation via In-context Conditioning
papers.abstract: Recent video generative models have shown strong capability in synthesizing high-quality and temporally coherent videos. Yet, adapting them for controllable portrait animation remains nontrivial, as existing methods typically rely on architectural changes or extra conditioning modules, increasing complexity and reducing compatibility with pretrained models. We present CatPortrait, a simple and effective framework that enables controllable portrait animation via 3D face guidance as in-context conditioning. CatPortrait preserves the original video generation backbone and injects structured 3D facial guidance into the input space through spatial concatenation, allowing pretrained image-to-video models to animate portraits without sacrificing their pretrained priors. CatPortrait supports both video-driven and audio-driven portrait animation within a unified framework. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CatPortrait achieves competitive or superior results across both settings.

papers.title: What Survives When Activation Steering Is Used as Memory
papers.abstract: Activation steering has recently been used as a memory for skills: past experiences of an agent are stored as steering vectors and retrieved later. Facts and preferences about the user are assumed to need text instead. We test that assumption with a training-free activation memory beside a frozen LLM. The change an experience causes in late-layer states is stored as a shift, filed under a whitened key for the conversation's gist, and added back in a later session only when the gist matches. We argue that such a shift is a fixed average of an effect that attention, in context, recomputes for every question, so only question-independent content can survive. In a pre-registered study on Qwen3.5-2B and 9B, with judges from four model families, the memory is selective (about 98% of unrelated replies are unchanged), but facts are stored as the word to say, in the last layers only, and are almost never used (at most 15% clean use, against 96-98% in context). Leanings transfer only in a narrow strength window. Most strikingly, the reference subtracted when writing a preference decides whether its concept or its direction survives: unless the opposite is subtracted, a stored dislike is recalled as a like.

papers.title: AlphaRLM: Aligning Language Models for Literature-Grounded Symbolic Factor Discovery
papers.abstract: Formulaic alpha mining seeks to discover executable expressions that capture predictive market signals in a vast, noisy search space. Recent LLM-based approaches use prompting, iterative search, or seed-factor evolution, leaving direct factor construction through policy learning less explored. To address this, we introduce AlphaRLM, a reinforcement-learning framework that trains LLMs to construct executable symbolic factors from financial literature without input factor expressions. AlphaRLM incorporates Literature-Guided Operator Assembly (LEGO), which conditions factor construction on literature-derived ideas and executable operators, providing semantic priors for exploration. It further aligns the generation policy with market feedback through executable-validity and grouped-return-separation rewards that capture non-monotonic structures across factor quantiles. Extensive experiments on CSI 300, CSI 1000, and S&P 500 show that AlphaRLM outperforms strong factor-mining and LLM-based baselines in annualized excess return. Notably, the 8B model achieves strong cross-market performance, highlighting the promise of literature-conditioned, market-aligned factor generation.

papers.title: Humans vs. Machines: A Comparison With AI Agents in Software Reverse Engineering
papers.abstract: Can an autonomous AI agent reverse engineer a binary as well as a skilled human analyst? Do they adopt the same strategy, and can agents scale to real-world programs? We compare human and LLM-based software reverse engineering (SRE): nine models tackle two compact static-analysis challenges previously solved by human analysts, scored with a common understanding rubric, and we record their complete interactions with IDA Pro. This lets us compare not only what humans and agents recover, but also how they investigate a binary. The best agents (GPT-5.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8, and Kimi K3) achieve statistically human-competitive understanding on both tasks, while weaker models remain far behind. Ablations show that the gap depends on code representation and workflow demands, not on model capability alone: open-weight models improve substantially with richer code representations, whereas frontier models show no significant change. Similar success rates hide different workflows. Humans repeatedly revisit functions and follow local program structure; strong agents jump across the binary, retrieve information broadly, and rarely return to inspected code, a behavior we call greedy fetching. This strategy is not fixed: given semantically richer code, agents fetch less without losing understanding. Because greedy fetching aggregates large amounts of code in the agent's context, we measure context-window saturation across 4,000 real-world binaries: large windows accommodate many programs, but larger applications and lower-level representations quickly exhaust them. Autonomous reverse engineering is becoming competitive, with a large speed advantage, but scaling it will require better navigation, selective retrieval, and persistent analysis state, not merely larger context windows.

papers.title: HiPAD: A Unified Gait, Audio-Visual, and Personality Fusion Network for Depression Detection, with a Hierarchical Personality Ablation and the Calibration Limits of Domain-Adapted LLMs
papers.abstract: We present HiPAD, a single fusion network submitted to all six sub-tracks of the MPDD-AVG 2026 depression-detection challenge, covering the Elder and Young cohorts and three modality sets (gait, audio-visual, and both), each combined with personality descriptions. The network encodes each available modality with a shared BiLSTM, zero-pads absent modalities, and applies cross-modal attention only when at least two of gait, audio and video are present. Personality, which dominates our results, is kept out of the attention and fused by concatenation. Because the architecture is identical in every sub-track, differences between them reflect the data rather than the model, and we use this to study three questions. Our main finding is that the personality description, roughly 150 tokens about who the subject is, carries more depression signal than audio, video, and gait combined: gait plus personality alone (TLS 0.647) beats every configuration that includes audio and video. First, a four-level ablation of the personality description (L0-L3) quantifies this: removing every personality-derived feature, including the Big Five scores that earlier MPDD ablations keep, lowers the Track-Level Score by 0.499 to 0.507 and leaves the model at chance. Second, domain-adapting the personality encoder with LoRA (7B) or QLoRA (72B) on PHQ-8/9 data raises binary Cohen's $κ$ by 0.13 but lowers the overall score by distorting the PHQ-9 regression; a frozen RoBERTa-large encoder does better at this sample size. Third, at fixed architecture, handcrafted clinical features (eGeMAPS, OpenFace action units) outperform generic deep features (wav2vec2, DenseNet) on the audio-visual tracks. The unified system reaches a cross-track G-Score of 0.482; with under 100 subjects per cohort, the limiting factors are the size of the representation and the calibration of the outputs, not the choice of architecture.

papers.title: Non-convex integer programming: a deterministic solution method of the large block sale problem
papers.abstract: We study a non-convex, nonlinear integer mathematical program with a linear constraint. This problem originates in finance and consists of selling a large predetermined quantity of a financial asset over a fixed time horizon, while maximizing the total proceeds. The selling price is modeled using a deterministic penalty function capturing the market's adverse reaction to the selling flow. From a complexity perspective, the problem is in NP. We first solve the problem exactly using dynamic programming and propose several heuristics that yield tight numerical lower bounds. We then reformulate the problem into an equivalent factorable form and derive a tight convex relaxation using McCormick inequalities. This relaxation is embedded within an adapted Branch & Bound algorithm to find the global optimum in finite time. Numerical experiments show that our methods outperform several widely used generic solvers (LocalSolver, Scip, Baron, Couenne, and Bonmin) for selected instances, but do not yield tight upper bounds, beyond small instances.

papers.title: AD-GS: Anatomical Density-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Dental CBCT Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Sparse-view Cone-Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) reconstruction is essential for reducing radiation dose and scan effort, but remains underconstrained due to limited projection information. Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based CBCT reconstruction methods rely on gradient-driven densification, which becomes unstable under sparse acquisition and often leads to over-smoothed structures. We propose AD-GS, an Anatomical Density-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that formulates Gaussian densification as an attenuation-aware Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling process. By interpreting Gaussians as samples from an underlying anatomical attenuation distribution, AD-GS adaptively concentrates representation capacity in high-attenuation regions, enabling sharper structural boundaries under sparse projections. To further constrain reconstruction, we incorporate a semantic regularization based on zero-shot features from Segment Anything in Medical Images, enforcing multi-view consistency through semantic priors. Experiments on the ToothFairy3 dental CBCT dataset demonstrate that AD-GS achieves superior structural fidelity and boundary preservation compared with existing 3DGS-based approaches under sparse-view settings within the dental and maxillofacial setting. Code is available at https://github.com/yulinjiaxue/AD-GS-BMVC2026.

papers.title: Cross-Material Magnetic Core Loss Prediction via Operating-Condition Matching and Partial Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Cross-material magnetic core loss prediction requires adapting to new material responses with limited measurements. Global feature alignment overlooks differences in source and target excitation coverage. This motivates selecting comparable samples and controlling each source measurement's alignment contribution. This paper proposes T-PCOT, a Transformer transfer method based on condition-supported partial optimal transport. Frequency, flux excursion, temperature, and waveform descriptors define a sparse graph of comparable operating conditions. A capacity-constrained transport plan distributes alignment across source measurements and leaves costly target mass unmatched. The plan is constructed from measured inputs before training and guides local waveform-feature consistency. An importance-weighted sampling scheme preserves both uniform source regression and the transport objective during minibatch optimization. Experiments on three material pairs and three target label budgets show that T-PCOT reduces mean relative error (MRE) and 95th-percentile error (P95) relative to Transformer-based multiple-kernel maximum mean discrepancy (T-MKMMD) in all nine comparisons. Macro MRE decreases from 12.60% to 9.65%, and macro P95 from 30.94% to 25.06%, corresponding to relative reductions of 23.41% and 19.01%. Controlled comparisons and ablations examine the roles of input processing, condition correspondence, and source capacity. The results demonstrate the predictive advantage of organizing cross-material alignment through operating-condition support over the compared global alignment method. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art predictive performance in magnetic core loss transfer learning.

papers.title: Risk-Constrained MPPI Tuning with Update-Aware MA-ES Racing
papers.abstract: We formulate offline tuning of Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) controllers as a chance-constrained black-box optimization problem and develop an update-aware framework based on Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (MA-ES). We use statistical information from noisy controller evaluations to determine when the evolutionary update is sufficiently reliable. When the recombination direction is certified, a derivative-free nonmonotone line search (NMLS) is used to refine the candidate solution, and a separate validation stage assesses the final frozen controller. We establish a worst-case arithmetic-complexity bound for both online MPPI control and offline tuning. Numerical experiments on TurtleBot 4, Jackal-like, and Ackermann models show that the proposed NMLS refinement is competitive with standard MA-ES, transfers across the three vehicle models without model-specific retuning, and improves several cost and validation measures. Both MA-ES variants also compare favorably with the tested randomized derivative-free line search (VRBBO) configuration. The results support the practical applicability and transferability of the proposed framework, while not claiming universal superiority or hardware-level safety.

papers.title: SkillHorizon: Constructing Long-Horizon Agent Tasks through Skill Composition
papers.abstract: Long-horizon agents must complete workflows in which later activities depend on earlier outputs and changes to shared state. A key challenge for evaluation is to expand task requirements and their dependencies while keeping tasks executable and outcomes verifiable. We introduce SkillHorizon, a benchmark that constructs long-horizon tasks through skill composition in seven business environments. Its generators use domain-specific rules to turn reusable skill procedures into concrete business activities. These activities are connected through input-output dependencies, shared resources, and state updates, allowing workload and coordination demands to grow together. Successful reference executions validate task feasibility and measure interaction workload, while programmatic evaluators assess local completion and whole-task success. We evaluate five language models on 1,050 tasks with reference interaction workloads ranging from 64K to 1M tokens. Across these scales, mean local-goal completion falls from 90.4% to 46.8%, as completed work fails to keep pace with growing requirements. At larger workloads, agents more often submit unsuccessful final answers with substantial work unfinished and tool-call allowance remaining. Trace analysis also identifies cases where scripts execute successfully but their outputs fail downstream business checks. SkillHorizon provides a configurable testbed for studying sustained progress, dependency coordination, and complete task delivery in growing workflows. Our code is available at https://github.com/KnowComp/SkillHorizon.

papers.title: A Minimal Theoretical Model for Morphodynamic Selection in Soft Matter Systems
papers.abstract: Soft matter systems often display shape transitions, mode competition, and threshold-like dynamical responses driven by the coupling between mechanics, geometry, and biochemical or active fields. Here we present a minimal theoretical framework for describing such morphodynamic selection using a small number of physically interpretable order parameters. The model combines elastic relaxation, active driving, and nonlinear feedback, yielding distinct regimes corresponding to weak deformation, single-mode selection, and coupled shape transformation. We derive the governing equations, identify the relevant dimensionless control parameters, and show how the phase behavior can be organized in terms of threshold competition and effective coupling strengths. The framework provides a compact route for connecting analytical theory, numerical simulations, and experimentally observable shape dynamics in soft and biological matter.

papers.title: SEEK: Agentic Knowledge Graph Retrieval for Secure Code Generation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate functionally correct code while introducing exploitable security weaknesses, particularly when developers specify functionality without explicit security requirements. Recent state-of-the-art approaches mitigate this problem using external security knowledge, but largely rely on flat similarity-based retrieval over independent artifacts, making it difficult to infer the relevant vulnerability space and retrieve targeted knowledge when direct matches are unavailable. We propose SEEK, an agentic Graph RAG framework for secure code generation that constructs a security knowledge graph using the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) taxonomy as its structural backbone and injects it with curated real-world CVE vulnerability-fix instances. At inference time, a Planner Agent predicts potential CWE weaknesses associated with the developer query, which guide Graph Scoping to restrict retrieval to relevant regions of the CWE taxonomy before deterministic multi-faceted candidate ranking. A Selection Agent subsequently validates the predicted weaknesses and retrieved candidates prior to code generation. Across five open-source LLMs, we evaluate SEEK in an out-of-distribution setting on CodeGuard+ and CyberSecEval, spanning C, C++, and Python. SEEK achieves the highest SecurePass@1 of 77.45% on CodeGuard+ and the highest aggregate ICD pass rate of 79.45% on CyberSecEval, surpassing prior approaches. Moreover, SEEK achieves 85.2% SecurePass@1 across 13 unseen CWE types with no directly linked vulnerability-fix instances, demonstrating strong generalizability, while maintaining acceptable inference latency costs.

papers.title: Allocative Efficiency and the Returns to Innovation
papers.abstract: Innovation changes welfare by improving technology and reallocating inputs across producers with different markups. When producers choose markups optimally, an innovator's own output and price adjustments have no private value at the margin, so reallocation affects its profit only through others' responses. For an innovator small in its markets, the change in allocative efficiency is of the same order as its cost saving but does not reach its profit. A process innovator is paid its cost saving, forgoing its own and downstream markups on added output. For U.S. public firms in 2015, these forgone markups average 26 percent of that saving. For innovators accounting for 56 percent of sales, allocative efficiency rises or falls by more than a tenth of their private return. With estimated spillovers, patenting firms' R&D has a social return 6.24 times its private return.

papers.title: FleetPilot: Fine-Grained Steering Empowers Real-World LLM Personalization
papers.abstract: With the rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs), there is an increasing demand for effective personalization techniques that can adapt model behavior to individual user preferences. Personalized LLMs must infer a user's query-dependent preferences from limited, heterogeneous, and evolving interaction histories. Existing approaches rely primarily on in-context personalization, parametric adaptation, or personalized reward modeling, but respectively incur recurring costs in context management, model optimization and deployment, or multi-candidate generation and scoring. These limitations become particularly restrictive when user observations are sparse and the preference evidence relevant to each query varies across contexts and over time. To address these challenges, we propose \modelname, a fine-grained and instance-tailored steering framework that dynamically generates sample-level interference vectors from user data and injects them into the model's forward pass for personalized adaptation. Our approach introduces: match contrast that produces user-relevant signals, fine-grained steering component that captures nuanced signals by hooking activations from attention and MLP layers, and query-conditioned aggregation module that synthesizes these signals into contextually relevant enhancements. Extensive experiments across diverse scenarios, including short-to-long text generation, and web function calling, validate the effectiveness and compatibility of \modelname. Results show that our method consistently brings significant performance gains, and show extreme superiority in fast-shifting and data-sparse environments. Additionally, \modelname rids us of training cycles and incurs light overhead of storage or inference latency. These make \modelname a strong and real-world deployable method. Implementation is available \footnote{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/FleetPilot}.

papers.title: HodgePhaseNet: Discrete Hodge Decomposition of Semantic Flows in Transformer Attention
papers.abstract: WavePhaseNet introduced frequency-resolved semantic representations, QuantumPhaseNet introduced gauge-covariant phase connections, and ModularPhaseNet made a finite cyclic phase channel and its cycle holonomy computable in an ordinary Transformer. These constructions are complementary, yet they do not by themselves separate an observed collection of pairwise relations into a globally consistent direction, circulation around local compositions, and circulation that persists around a larger unfilled cycle. HodgePhaseNet addresses this separation by representing semantic transitions as an antisymmetric real-valued 1-cochain on a finite oriented simplicial complex. With vertex-edge incidence matrix $B_1$ and edge-face incidence matrix $B_2$, every such field has a unique orthogonal decomposition $Ω= B_1^TΦ+ B_2Ψ+ H$, where $B_1H=0$ and $B_2^TH=0$. The three component fields are unique even when their potentials are not. We give explicit projectors, a sparse implementation, integrability and gauge results, a verified numerical example, and a redesigned attention interface. The attention bias is defined on allowed ordered query-key pairs, remains consistent under arbitrary choices of edge orientation, and preserves a decoder's causal information boundary by constructing its complex from the visible prefix. Gauge invariance of the attention output is conditional on using invariant or appropriately compensated features. A simple difference of vertex embeddings has no coexact or harmonic component; a genuine relation encoder is therefore indispensable. Local circulation is not automatically contradiction, and harmonic flow is not automatically missing knowledge. These interpretations and any reduction in factual error require controlled empirical evaluation. This paper presents a mathematical and architectural proposal, not external natural-language performance results.

papers.title: Strong Stable Manifolds and Uniqueness of Parabolic Rays in the Newtonian $N$-Body Problem
papers.abstract: We study uniqueness of parabolic motions in the Newtonian $N$-body problem using strong stable manifolds and direct action comparisons. Fix a minimal normalized central configuration $c$, with no nondegeneracy assumption. In McGehee coordinates, every parabolic motion with this limiting configuration has a tail on the outgoing strong stable manifold. Its local graph yields a smooth velocity field on a truncated cone, selecting a collision-free parabolic motion that stays in the cone and is unique among all such cone-confined motions. For free-time minimizing rays, an explicit renormalized action excess gives a no-exit estimate, hence uniqueness from a smaller cone without a confinement assumption. Together with known existence results, these cone theorems imply that every $c$-parabolic motion has a tail that is a $c$-parabolic geodesic ray. Globally, we propagate the stable graph backward and compare the excess on its regular branches. An endpoint differential formula and Sard's theorem imply that the configurations admitting more than one such minimizing ray form a Lebesgue-null set. The uniqueness proofs combine local dynamics and variational comparisons without using differentiability of a global Hamilton--Jacobi solution.

papers.title: A lower bound on $\text{depth} \ \mathbf{A/I^n}$
papers.abstract: Let $(A,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $I\subseteq \mathfrak{m}$ be an ideal in $A$. Let $\ell(I)$ be the analytic spread of $I$. Let $G_I(A) = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0}I^n/I^{n+1}$ be the associated graded ring of $I$ and let its depth be $t$. We prove $\text{depth} \ A/I^n \geq t - \ell(I)$ for all $n\geq 1$.

papers.title: Ensemble-Based Modelling of Optogenetic Bioprocesses under Phototoxicity
papers.abstract: Optogenetics enables methanol-free protein production in the yeast $\textit{Komagataella phaffii}$ using light as a control input, facilitated by the blue-light-responsive transcription factor EL222. This opens the door to more programmable protein production in the food and biopharmaceutical industries. However, excessive illumination can inhibit growth and protein accumulation in some of these engineered cell factories. Previous hybrid modelling used black-box regression across sparsely sampled conditions to infer light-dependent kinetic parameters, without explicitly representing intracellular regulation. Here, we develop a multiscale mechanistic model linking EL222 activation, transcription, and translation to protein, biomass, and substrate dynamics. A latent light-associated stress state represents photoinhibitory effects on growth, transcription, and translation. An ensemble-based parameter-estimation strategy combines repeated global-local optimisation with screening for parameter sets supporting locally stable intracellular steady states under specified light conditions. Using available batch data for yeast-enhanced green fluorescent protein production in a $\textit{K. phaffii}$ strain carrying eight EL222 gene copies, the ensemble-mean predictions captured the main experimental trends in protein accumulation and growth across six constant light intensities. Parameter variability was propagated to time-course predictions, providing an empirical assessment of parameter-related uncertainty. Wider prediction bands coincided with less complete experimental coverage of the growth phases. Overall, the framework provides a mechanistic basis for future model-based optimisation and control of optogenetic bioprocesses under phototoxicity.

papers.title: A Unified Kalman-Type Classification of Controllability for Linear Stochastic Systems
papers.abstract: We provide a unified algebraic classification of approximate controllability, approximate null controllability, exact null controllability, and exact controllability for finite-dimensional linear stochastic control systems with constant coefficients and multidimensional Brownian noise. The controls may enter both the drift and the diffusion terms, and the joint diffusion-control matrix may have arbitrary rank. A finite decreasing sequence of subspaces defines a common geometric obstruction. Its vanishing characterizes the two approximate properties and exact null controllability. Exact controllability to arbitrary random targets additionally requires the joint diffusion-control matrix to be surjective. The codimension of the obstruction is given by a rank difference of explicit polynomial block matrices, yielding finite tests in the original coefficients. When the joint diffusion-control matrix is surjective, we obtain a finite Kalman-type full-rank condition for exact controllability. If the obstruction vanishes, a linear state feedback with a deterministic time-dependent gain drives every initial state to zero at any prescribed positive time with finite energy and polynomial small-time cost. An equivalent orthogonal elimination algorithm computes the rank differences with polynomial storage and cost, avoiding exponentially large block matrices. A two-noise example relates the input classification to terminal errors and control energy in penalized stochastic linear-quadratic control problems.

papers.title: Metric-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Object Hallucination Reduction in LVLM-Based Image Captioning
papers.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have excelled in joint visual and language understanding, particularly in image captioning. However, LVLMs remain prone to object hallucination, describing non-existent entities in the given image. Previous remedies, including dataset-enhanced supervised training and reinforcement learning from human feedback, show promise but rely heavily on costly human involvement, limiting scalability. To address this, we propose a reinforcement learning framework to mitigate object hallucination in LVLM-based image captioning, driven entirely by natural language processing (NLP) metrics. While optimizing reinforcement learning solely on NLP metrics offers scalability, it also introduces pitfalls: reward hacking, sparse feedback, and costly training. Our framework sidesteps these by introducing an Object Consistency Score (OCS) capturing both correctness and coverage of objects, incorporating KL-regularization for denser token-level guidance, and designing a lightweight PPO variant that fine-tunes adapters atop a frozen LVLM backbone, achieving efficiency and stability. Extensive experiments on the InstructBLIP baseline demonstrate the effectiveness and generalizability of our framework, achieving a substantial hallucination reduction of up to 41\% on the COCO dataset and 29\% on the Visual Genome. Furthermore, the framework can enhance caption quality by incorporating complementary evaluation metrics such as BERTScore and METEOR. These results reveal a broader insight in multimodal learning: LVLMs can effectively self-correct hallucinations using metric feedback, motivating deeper exploration into scalable reinforcement frameworks that significantly reduce human effort.

papers.title: EnactOpt: Diagnosis-Guided Harness Evolution for Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Embodied agents built on foundation models rely on an execution harness to organize observations, guide actions, and incorporate execution feedback into subsequent decisions. Failures can arise not only from limited model capabilities, but also from how the harness presents evidence and guides its use. These model-external mechanisms provide an adaptation target without updating model parameters, but task-specific interaction experience can be costly to collect. Task-level outcomes alone do not reveal whether relevant evidence was missing from the model input or was available but inadequately used. Moreover, these two aspects are coupled: effective action guidance may require evidence that the current context omits, while exposing that evidence alone does not ensure an appropriate response. We introduce EnactOpt, which uses limited execution feedback to jointly evolve reusable textual skills and context-construction code while keeping the underlying models and runtime fixed. It diagnoses adjacent decisions by relating action feedback to the actual model input and subsequent action. Structured episode summaries guide joint revisions through prompt-level edit operators, and candidate harnesses undergo compatibility checks and validation-based retention. Across VLABench, ALFWorld, and Embodied Agent Interface (EAI), EnactOpt improves task success by approximately 10-27 percentage points over the initial harnesses and outperforms the evaluated GEPA, TextGrad, and Trace2Skill baselines. These gains extend to task conditions not used for harness evolution or candidate selection. The results support a complementary route to embodied adaptation: turning limited execution experience into reusable behavioral improvements by jointly refining how evidence is presented and acted upon.

papers.title: Uniqueness and stability for inverse potential scattering with multiple wavenumbers
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the inverse scattering problem of determining a real-valued potential for the three-dimensional Schrödinger equation from multi-wavenumber data. Under suitable a priori bounds, we establish local increasing stability from near-field Dirichlet data on a fixed sphere for polynomially decaying potentials, and global increasing stability from full far-field amplitudes for exponentially decaying potentials. The stability estimates consist of a noise term and a remainder term, with the latter decreasing as the upper measured wavenumber increases. We also obtain global uniqueness from exact near-field data under weaker regularity assumptions. The analysis combines analytic continuation, weighted resolvent estimates, and half-ray identities whose differences at chord endpoints cancel the unknown exterior contribution.

papers.title: Sharp bounds and extremal structure of minimally strongly $k$-connected digraphs
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a finite simple minimally strongly $k$-connected digraph, where $k\ge 2$, and let $n=|V(D)|$. Mader proved in 1985 that $|A(D)|\le 2k(n-k)$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with equality if and only if $D\cong \overleftrightarrow{K}_{k,n-k}$ (JCTB 1985). We prove that this bound holds whenever $n\ge 3k-1$ and that the order threshold $3k-1$ is best possible. Moreover, if $n\ge 3k$, then equality holds if and only if $D\cong \overleftrightarrow{K}_{k,n-k}$. The threshold $3k$ is also best possible. These results resolve the conjecture of Mader in (JCTB 1985).

papers.title: Single-Sample Decoding of a Two-Layer Sound-Word Canvas Model for Thai Klon Pad
papers.abstract: We present a generator of Thai klon pad verse, one stanza from a short topic, and evaluate it against human verse on held-out topics. The generator is a masked language model initialised from WangchanBERTa over a fixed canvas with two layers: a sound layer of pronounced syllables, where rhyme, tone and syllable count are enforced as hard masks, and a word layer of whole words, so that no word is cut into written pieces. Decoding commits one cell at a time and samples at temperature 0.4; one sample is drawn per topic, with no selection, reranking or repair. On 78 held-out topics never used in development, judged by three independent runs of a frozen LLM judge in the same pools as the human stanzas from which the topics were written, 70.5% of the generated stanzas pass form, lexical cleanness of all four lines and topic alignment together, against 76.9% for the human stanzas (difference -6.4 points, 95% CI [-19.2, +6.4]). Cleanness is level with human (85.9% vs. 87.2%), and the stanzas pass form and cleanness together slightly more often than the human ones (+3.8 points, [-6.4, +14.1]); the difference lies in alignment (84.6% vs. 91.0%), on topics that were written from the human stanzas. The low temperature matters: at higher temperatures the same model passes clearly fewer of the same topics, because lexical errors lie in the model's lower-probability choices; sharpening the sampling distribution removes most of them, at a cost in vocabulary (7.5% rare words against 16.5% in the human stanzas) and diversity. The pre-registered target, all-three within 5 points of human, is missed by 1.4 points. KlonSuphap-LM, the only public klon pad generator we know of, passes none of the 78 held-out topics when judged in separate pools together with the method's and the human stanzas (form 19.2%, cleanness 3.8%).

papers.title: A proof of Kahane's conjecture in the Wiener algebra
papers.abstract: We prove Kahane's conjecture: if a continuous unimodular function $F$ on the circle satisfies $\|F^n\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}=o(\log|n|)$ as $|n|\to\infty$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, then $F(x)=e^{i(mx+b)}$ for some $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}$. The main step is a logarithmic lower bound for averages: for every nonconstant real-valued $\varphi\in A(\mathbb{T})$, $\frac{1}{T}\int_a^{a+T}\|e^{it\varphi}\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}dt \ge c_\varphi\log T \quad(a\in\mathbb{R},\ T\ge T_\varphi)$, where $c_\varphi>0$ and $T_\varphi>1$ are independent of $a$. The proof uses exact sampling on finite subgroups of the circle, uniformly bounded localized modulations, and the weighted non-harmonic Littlewood inequality of Jaming--Kellay--Saba. A suitable cutoff and a small linear perturbation of the phase ensure that a fixed positive proportion of the coefficients at the beginning of the frequency ordering have modulus one. Passing to integer powers and removing the degree of the circle map yield Kahane's conjecture without any additional smoothness assumptions. We also give equivalent phase, convolution, and operator formulations, and derive consequences for homomorphisms of weighted Wiener algebras and for higher-dimensional tori.

papers.title: Fitting Every Hint Is Not Enough: Premature Floods in Recurrent Algorithmic Reasoners
papers.abstract: Recurrent algorithmic reasoners are trained with per-step hints on small graphs and run for many more steps on large ones. On breadth-first search in SALSA-CLRS, we find that a reasoner can reproduce every training hint and still fail on deep graphs: after some exact steps, it declares nodes reached before the search gets there. We call this a premature flood and trace two routes to it. In our GRU processor with a degree input, the flood is carried in the hidden state and set off when that input is in the tail of the training distribution. Setting the input higher at inference brings the flood sooner, and none of the six flooding models counts steps. Without the input, summing the neighbors' states instead of averaging them also breaks the processor. In the benchmark's own GIN and PGN, trained with its code, some seeds instead flood from a fixed step, on sparse and dense graphs alike. Clamping the degree input or adding 200 dense training graphs removes every failure of the GRU processor. Detaching the state between steps avoids the flood in that processor (0 of 23 seeds, against 6 under full backpropagation) but not with sums or a residual update, and two published remedies leave floods. None of the benchmark's test sets is both deep and dense, but its deepest one shows the second route: on its Delaunay graphs at 1,600 nodes, one GIN seed floods from step 18. We therefore recommend auditing the range of every input and aggregate, which catches the first route, and testing on deep graphs, which catches both.

papers.title: Surfactant-induced Marangoni stresses and surface viscosity in Faraday instability
papers.abstract: We investigate the influence of insoluble-surfactant elasticity and Boussinesq-Scriven surface viscosity on the parametric instability of an interface separating two viscous fluids. The two-fluid Floquet formulation of Kumar& Tuckerman (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 279, 1994, pp. 49-68) is extended to include surfactant transport, Marangoni stresses and surface viscosity. For the parameter range considered, both mechanisms increase the onset acceleration relative to the clean interface state, but through distinct responses: Marangoni elasticity produces a non-monotonic threshold, whereas surface viscosity yields a monotonic increase towards saturation. Analysis of the corresponding unforced gravity-capillary modes shows that both mechanisms modify modal damping and natural frequency. Wavenumber selection reduces the detuning from subharmonic resonance by approximately an order of magnitude relative to that evaluated at the clean interface critical wavenumber. Along the selected branches, variations in the onset acceleration closely follow those in modal damping, with residual detuning playing a secondary role. Despite their distinct interfacial stress mechanisms, both Marangoni elasticity and surface viscosity suppress tangential interfacial motion in the strong-rheology limit, approaching a common tangentially immobilized condition.

papers.title: Too Late to Prune: Generative AI, the Screen, and Team Creative Decisions
papers.abstract: Generative AI makes options cheap and shifts the bottleneck of creative work from generating options to screening them. We argue that AI's value depends on whether its options arrive before or after the team's screen. In our model, early options compete for a place in the portfolio; late options arrive after that competition and are kept unscreened. In a preregistered experiment, we randomly assigned 148 three-person teams to five schedules of access to the same language model during a product-design task with timed search and selection stages. Moving the same 15 minutes of access from search to selection lowered expert-rated creativity by 0.62 standard deviations, although teams used the model at similar rates. Platform logs locate the difference at the screen. Early access enlarged the pool of ideas fivefold, and teams pruned it. Late-access teams reached the screen with the same small pool as teams without AI and then searched again, devoting 29% of their selection-stage queries to generating new options, compared with 11% for teams with access throughout. Late access added breadth, not quality: these teams submitted 73% more proposals than did teams without AI. Language-model judges detected the benefit of access but not the cost of late timing.

papers.title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank II: Generalizing Linusson's count to sumsets of f-vectors
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra of an $n$-dimensional vector space over a field, let $F$ be a graded free $E$-module with $r$ generators of degrees $d_1 \le \dots \le d_r$, and let $M$ range over the monomial submodules of Amata and Crupi. The Hilbert function of $F/M$ is a shifted sum of $f$-vectors of simplicial complexes; the companion paper determines the convex hull of such sums, and here we count them. For $r = 1$ the count is Linusson's (1999); we show that no new recursion is needed for general $r$. Using two statistics of an $f$-vector -- its top nonvanishing degree and the initial degree of the corresponding ideal -- we prove that the number of achievable Hilbert functions is a product of $r-1$ transfer matrices, one per generator-degree gap, with entries differences of Linusson's refined counts $E^p(n,k)$. The rank enters only as the length of a matrix product. The same holds for the proper variant. Consequences: a linear recurrence in $r$ for constant gaps, with exact exponential asymptotics $K λ^r$ when the gap is positive; polynomiality in $r$ when all gaps vanish; a threshold beyond which the count is a plain power; and polynomiality in the number of vertices.

papers.title: Time-temperature-composition equivalence of the glass transition in digitally mixed 3D-printed polymers
papers.abstract: For more than seventy years, time-temperature equivalence (TTE) has enabled a few measurements to describe the linear viscoelasticity of polymers over many decades of frequency. Multimaterial 3D printing now combines elastomeric and glassy resins voxel by voxel into digitally mixed polymers. Composition shifts the glass transition along the frequency axis, as temperature does, but also broadens it and increases the rubbery plateau modulus. A translation, the only operation of TTE, cannot capture these changes. Here we establish a time-temperature-composition equivalence (TTCE) from dynamic mechanical measurements of five compositions of a printed family. A shift of the transition along the reduced-frequency axis, a stretch of its breadth and a normalization between its plateaus collapse the storage modulus onto one master curve. The collapse holds at every measured temperature, frequency and composition, through a single reduced variable. The position and breadth of the transition change linearly with the volume fraction of the glassy resin. The phase angle and the relaxation spectrum superpose with the same parameters, so the family shares one distribution of relaxation times. The resulting closed form gives the storage and loss moduli continuously in composition, temperature and frequency, and quantitatively predicts two further mixtures withheld from the calibration. The same shift, stretch and normalization also collapse published temperature sweeps of a patterned composite family of different resins, pointing to broader applicability. Composition thus joins temperature and frequency as a third variable of one equivalence, and the closed form can guide the design of graded and architected printed structures.

papers.title: The $R$-Process Alliance: On J0010$-$1735, an Accreted, Chemically Unusual, Metal-poor Star with $R$-process Enhancement
papers.abstract: We present a detailed chemo-dynamical analysis of the chemically peculiar very metal-poor ([Fe/H]$=-2.22\pm 0.11$) Milky Way (MW) halo star, 2MASS J00101758$-$1735387 (hereafter J0010-1735), discovered by the $R$-Process Alliance. We derive abundances for 45 elements, including 28 neutron-capture elements, and confirm that \thestar\ is highly $r$-process-enhanced, with [Eu/Fe]=$+1.30$. The light, $α$, and Fe-peak element abundances ratios relative to Fe are all sub-solar, aside from C, Si, and most extremely, Ca. We investigate three possible formation scenarios based on the star's chemical abundances and orbital kinematics: whether it formed in the \textit{in-situ} MW halo, in a MW dwarf galaxy satellite, or in a satellite of the Magellanic Cloud system. Using the position of \thestar\ in the [Mg/Mn]--[Al/Fe] plane, the abundance pattern of both the light and heavy elements, and the kinematics, we conclude that J0010-1735 most plausibly originated in a now-disrupted ultra-faint dwarf galaxy that was accreted into the MW halo. We examine potential chemical enrichment scenarios of J0010-1735, including one similar to the $r$-process-enhanced UFD Reticulum II, or enrichment via a sub-Chandrasekhar Type Ia SNe, potentially supplemented by a Ca-rich gap transient and by a separate neutron-rich site that facilitated $r$-process enrichment. A nuclear cosmochronometric age of $12.5\pm4.2$ Gyr is derived from the [Th/Eu] ratio, consistent with an ancient origin in one of the earliest star-forming systems in the universe.

papers.title: Mixing Regularization for Average-Reward $Q$-Learning and $Q$-Planning
papers.abstract: The average-reward setting for reinforcement learning is challenging because its Bellman operator is known to contract in span only when the underlying Markov chain is mixing. Whereas existing work typically assumes a contraction property, e.g., through environment mixing, we consider the setting where we are given a reward-agnostic $m$-step mixing policy, and we control the contraction and exploration properties of the learned policy by regularizing toward the mixing policy. We provide finite-time analysis of $Q$-learning algorithms that can be instantiated with multiple choices of regularization, with guarantees measured with respect to the regularized fixed point. Our framework exposes novel regularizer-dependent objects that control contraction, exploration, and operator bias. In the one-step setting, our rates match the best known rates for $Q$-iteration and synchronous $Q$-learning, and for $m$-step mixing we derive new rates. We also study $Q$-planning variants, and show that planning acts as time-localized learning, where the planning horizon $H$ trades off the bias from the boundary value against the sample complexity. Finally, we present numerical studies validating the analysis: (i) knowledge of a strong mixing policy improves convergence and exploration, and its advantage increases with bottleneck severity and, (ii) our theory predicts the convergence and bias rankings of regularizers from the $α$-divergence family.

papers.title: Characterizing the Separability Gap in Prior-Data Fitted Networks
papers.abstract: Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) are transformers pretrained on simulated datasets to approximate Bayesian posterior predictive distributions. Standard PFN theory assumes a separable task prior, under which the feature distribution and the mechanism generating labels from features are independent. We show that common PFN priors are non-separable, even in simple settings. Consequently, standard pretraining targets a predictive distribution based on a task posterior updated using both the labeled context and the query features. We characterize its difference from the predictive based on the context posterior alone and show that this difference vanishes under posterior concentration. Under misspecification (i.e., when the true joint distribution lies outside the prior's support), however, prior non-separability can favor better feature fit at the expense of conditional label fit. We illustrate the consequences for feature attribution, Bayesian optimization, and martingale checks of Bayesian behavior. The same dependence also enables PFNs to learn from additional unlabeled observations. We demonstrate this with SemiTabICL, a PFN explicitly pretrained to use these observations, which improves accuracy over a matched supervised baseline. Our findings highlight the need for explicit rules on unlabeled data use in PFN evaluation and establish the dependence between feature and label distributions as a consequential prior design choice.

papers.title: Uniform Green packing on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We extend the packing results of Etayo, Hedenmalm, and Ortega-Cerda for complex tori to arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces. The construction uses two different approaches, one based on complex geometry of line bundles, and the other on Laplace designs. Both approaches give the same basic existence of close-to-optimal point configurations on the given surface. This version was written with the help of ChatGPT.

papers.title: Affine realization of tilted Richardson varieties
papers.abstract: Richardson varieties provide geometric representatives for products of Schubert classes, with stratifications indexed by the subintervals of Bruhat intervals. We construct analogous geometric models for tilted Bruhat intervals for all split connected reductive groups. Our construction uses Richardson varieties in affine flag varieties and yields abstract tilted Richardson varieties whose isomorphism classes, together with their labeled stratifications, are independent of the choices involved. We obtain an explicit formula for the point-counting polynomials of their open parts in terms of increasing minimal weight paths, extending Dyer's formula for Kazhdan--Lusztig $R$-polynomials. Over the real numbers, their totally nonnegative parts are regular CW complexes homeomorphic to closed balls, which gives a natural geometric realization of the posets of tilted Bruhat subintervals in all Lie types. Over the complex numbers, we prove that their fundamental classes push forward under a continuous loop evaluation map to the Poincaré duals of the minimal-degree coefficients of quantum Schubert products.

papers.title: EpNet-Si: Atomic Form Factors Learned from Band Structures
papers.abstract: The empirical pseudopotential method (EPM) computes band structures with one diagonalization per $k$ point and no self-consistency, but its fixed atomic form factors do not transfer between crystal structures. To address this limitation, we introduce EpNet-Si, an EPM for silicon in which an equivariant network predicts each atom's plane-wave form factor from its local environment: a species potential plus monopole, dipole and quadrupole corrections, mixed by a learned router over atomic densities, together with an $s/p$ nonlocal projector. With 6{,}195 parameters, the model is trained through the eigensolver on reference density functional theory (DFT) band energies of only 77 cells. Among 231 distortions of the trained structure types, the 142 gapped cells have mean band and gap errors of 15 and 8\,meV; among 192 unseen structures, the 165 gapped cells have mean errors of 38 and 49\,meV. Physical properties derived from EpNet-Si, including effective masses, gap pressure coefficients, deformation potentials and the density of states at the Fermi level, agree with those obtained from the reference DFT calculations. These results suggest that the classical EPM, fitted to a small set of reference data, can be extended into a fast alternative for modern electronic band-structure calculations.

papers.title: Learning Where to Split: Dynamic Band Splitting for Audio Source Separation
papers.abstract: Audio source separation models must preserve fine spectral structure while keeping the cost of the separator tractable. Band-split architectures reduce this cost by manually partitioning the spectrum into predefined frequency bands and encoding each band as a token, but the same boundaries are used for every mixture. Because informative spectral structure varies with source content, fixed boundaries can merge discriminative components or spend tokens where little resolution is needed. We introduce Dynamic Band Splitting (DBS), an end-to-end framework that adapts boundary locations and band widths to each mixture under a fixed band-token budget. DBS predicts content-conditioned boundary scores within frequency blocks, selects a prescribed number of boundaries using hard Top-$K$, and applies content-dependent pooling to obtain compact band tokens. After separation, it smooths and expands these tokens to the original STFT grid, refines them along frequency, and decodes complex masks with a frequency-shared head. DBS improved separation over the corresponding static models on DnR v2, MUSDB18-HQ, and EchoSet, with DBS-BSRNN achieving relative gain of 29.0% in average SI-SDR on DnR v2. These results and boundary analyses on DnR v2 show that content-adaptive frequency partitioning benefits multiple separator backbones under a fixed band-token budget. Code and audio demos are available at https://cslikai.cn/Dynamic-Band-Splitting

papers.title: Best-of-Both-Worlds Fair Division via Subsidies
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between fair division with $\textit{subsidies}$ and $\textit{best-of-both-worlds}$ (BoBW) fairness for indivisible items. We prove a general reduction of BoBW existence to envy-freeability. Specifically, for any scale-free ex-post property $P$ (e.g., EF1, EFX, PO) and any scale-free valuation class $\mathcal{V}$ (e.g, additive, submodular, subadditive, monotone), if every instance in $\mathcal{V}$ admits a $P$-allocation that can be made envy-free using subsidies, then every such instance admits an ex-ante envy-free lottery supported on $P$-allocations. The proof uses linear programming duality. As applications, the reduction gives alternative proofs of BoBW existence results for additive goods, chores, and mixtures of goods and chores. The converse of our general reduction holds for two agents but fails for three: We provide a four-good counterexample with monotone submodular valuations where an ex-ante envy-free and ex-post EF1 lottery exists, but no allocation is simultaneously EF1 and envy-freeable. For lexicographic valuations, we prove simultaneous EFX, Pareto optimality, and envy-freeability (and hence BoBW guarantees for EFX+PO) for three agents, and show that even EFX and envy-freeability can be incompatible for four agents.

papers.title: Optimally Setting RMS Energy Bands for Detecting Oscillations
papers.abstract: Oscillation monitors have root-mean-square (RMS) energy detectors at their core. These detect oscillation in a predefined frequency band by comparing the signal power in that band with a threshold (usually set empirically). A key design decision is the choice of frequency bands. Traditionally, for monitoring the stability of wide-area electromechanical modes, finer bands were set below 1 Hz, while higher frequencies were covered by wider bands. However, this approach can yield poor detection in modern power systems with fast and largely unknown local dynamics. This letter proposes an algorithm to set frequency bands from the ambient noise spectrum to maximize the average detection performance.

papers.title: Certify the Decision, Not Every Score: Exact Top-k Selection from Few Evaluations
papers.abstract: Choosing a few robust algorithms or schedules can require evaluating every candidate under many adverse scenarios, even though an agent only needs to identify the winners. A predictor may suggest those winners, but cannot rule out a surprise in an unevaluated scenario. We introduce Certified Adaptive Selection (CAS), which returns the exact top-$k$ set as soon as remaining uncertainty cannot change it. CAS keeps guaranteed lower and upper bounds on Expected Shortfall (ES), the average loss in the worst scenarios. Its stopping test compares the worst admissible selected candidate with the best admissible excluded one; for information-disjoint Cartesian intervals this one-cut test is necessary and sufficient. Prediction has a separate role: selecting the next outcome to evaluate, never authorizing the decision. For empirical ES with exact unit-cost queries, we compute in polynomial time the fewest evaluations that could have proved the realized decision in hindsight. Our prediction-guided agent CAS-PG is exact for every predictor, including adversarial ones. On two public algorithm-selection matrices, CAS-PG certifies the exact top three after 630 of 3150 and 981 of 2200 replayed queries, or $1.14$ and $1.18$ times that hindsight minimum. Without historical outcomes, its transcript-only variant requires $1.28$ and $1.37$ times the minimum, outperforming the tested non-predictive certified policies. Separately, a prediction-free CAS policy avoids $93.0\%$ of exact recourse solves in synthetic energy scheduling. One certificate thus supports several acquisition policies and separately proved risk/cost extensions: prediction changes the work, not the justified choice.

papers.title: Barrier-Constrained Guidance For Real-time Asynchronous VLA Execution
papers.abstract: While asynchronous execution enables VLA models to operate in real-time environments by predicting the next chunk during execution, it inevitably introduces boundary misalignment with the committed action stream. Existing delay-aware solutions address this at the prohibitive cost of extensive retraining, architectural modifications, or fixed-prefix inpainting that inflates computation when low latency is vital. To address these problems, we propose FreeBar, a training-free real-time inference plugin that enables robust asynchronous execution with only marginal additional inference cost by casting chunk alignment in flow-based VLAs as barrier-guided action-space constraint. Specifically, FreeBar introduces a lightweight Control Barrier Function (CBF)-inspired consistency constraint between consecutive action chunks and solves the resulting correction in closed form, avoiding costly backpropagation through the VLA action head. By progressively tightening the consistency bound during generation, FreeBar aligns generated chunks with the committed execution stream while preserving early-stage generative and within-chunk future action flexibility,. Across Kinetix, RoboCasa, and diverse real-world robotic platforms with multiple VLA backbones, FreeBar improves success rates over naive asynchronous execution by 10%--15% on average, with larger gains in highly dynamic scenarios. It also preserves real-time computational efficiency, decreasing inference latency per action chunk over 45% than RTC. Additionally, as a universal plugin, FreeBar remains robust across distinct latency environments, base policies, and hyperparameter settings.

papers.title: Recurrent In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models adapt to new datasets through in-context learning (ICL), and, like most transformers, they tie computational depth to the number of independently parameterized layers. We ask whether the ICL stage of such a model needs a distinct set of parameters for every layer, or only depth. We introduce Tab-Loop, which replaces the 12 untied ICL blocks of TabICLv2 with 4 tied blocks applied $k$ times and changes nothing else: the encoders, decoder, synthetic prior and training recipe are shared with an untied baseline trained for the same compute. At matched pretraining compute (18.2 EFLOP) and matched inference compute (12 block applications), Tab-Loop matches the baseline with 62\% fewer parameters (10.4M vs.\ 27.6M): held-out log loss is 0.4583 vs.\ 0.4588, mean accuracy on 200 TALENT datasets is 84.10\% vs.\ 83.92\%, and Elo on 38 TabArena datasets is 1409 vs.\ 1396. A 4-block untied control with Tab-Loop's parameter count, which sees 32\% more training tables for the same compute, trails both (83.46\%; Elo 1343). Because weights are shared, depth becomes a choice made at inference. Accuracy rises with the number of loops through the trained range and holds beyond it, and continued training with deeper loops extends the useful range, reaching the baseline's stage-2 scores at 4--5$\times$ its inference compute. At this scale, the ICL stage of a tabular foundation model needs depth more than it needs distinct parameters.

papers.title: DiffGA: Steering Frozen Diffusion Models for Materials Design via Evolutionary Search
papers.abstract: Steering candidate generation toward user-defined objectives is central to inverse materials design, yet remains difficult when objectives are black-box, changing, or non-differentiable, as in many simulation- and experiment-derived properties. Generative models offer a solution but typically require retraining or fine-tuning for each new objective, demanding labeled data and substantial compute, or rely on differentiable guidance that is brittle to gradient noise and undefined for many practical targets. We present DiffGA, a retraining-free framework that injects evolutionary search into the sampling trajectory of a retrained diffusion model, evolving partially denoised states under an arbitrary black-box oracle. Because oracle evaluation often dominates campaign cost, we couple DiffGA with an on-the-fly Bayesian surrogate that reuses representations from state-of-the-art machine-learned force fields (MLFFs). A Gaussian process is fit during the campaign on the force fields's graph embeddings and, once it demonstrably ranks an unseen generation, replaces expensive property evaluations under an uncertainty-aware acquisition rule, reducing oracle cost with negligible loss of accuracy. Across three crystal-design tasks using a frozen MatterGen backbone, DiffGA outperforms diffusion-only, compute-matched, purely evolutionary, and fine-tuned baselines in oracle-assessed rates of stable, unique, and novel hits. Rather than proposing scientific compounds, we use density functional theory to quantify MLFF oracle fidelity, showing that it is a faithful proxy in key regimes but systematically biased in others, delineating when proxy-driven generative discovery can be trusted. On a representative sample, DiffGA's top hits survive first principles re-evaluation as physically realistic hits, while the surrogate-accelerated pipeline preserves this fidelity at a fraction of the cost.

papers.title: Bayesian adaptive design for neural recruitment curves
papers.abstract: Nonlinear response models remain ubiquitous across disciplines with recruitment curves describing muscle response to neural stimulation. Conventional acquisition methods typically rely on static uniform sampling, requiring many stimuli, while adaptive threshold-hunting designs such as ML-PEST forfeit accurate characterization of the overall curve. We present a Bayesian adaptive design that uses posterior uncertainty over curve parameters to propose stimuli that maximize information gain across the full recruitment curve. We additionally implement a focused acquisition method that can target arbitrary subset of curve parameters, which we use to evaluate and interpret our design. In simulations, our design outperforms uniform sampling in recovering threshold while matching ML-PEST, and outperforms ML-PEST in predictive curve accuracy while matching uniform. It likewise matches our threshold-focused acquisition, suggesting our design doesn't trade off threshold estimation for recovering the curve. We further show data collected using our design yields greater power when detecting a change in threshold in intervention studies. Our design proposes the next stimulus within 5 seconds, making it feasible for transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) experiments. Finally, we validate our design in TMS experiments and provide a library for Python, called onMEP, for online acquisition of neural recruitment curves.

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of a Collaborative Teleoperation Interface for Multi-Operator Multi-Robot Systems in Challenging Environments
papers.abstract: Multi-robot systems that combine the complementary capabilities of specialised platforms are critical for complex missions in challenging, inaccessible environments. Current deployments assign an operator or operator team to each robot, with collaboration relying on operator-to-operator communication to manually coordinate heterogeneous platforms with incompatible interfaces. This operator-dependent approach increases cognitive load and limits scalability across robots from different manufacturers. This study designs and evaluates a shared-visualisation collaborative teleoperation interface to improve operator coordination, situational awareness, and the task performance in multi-operator, multi-robot systems. A comparative user study with 16 participants compared three teleoperation conditions: co-located operators with a shared interface, remote operators with a shared interface, and co-located operators with individual interfaces. Participants controlled two simulated robots in a nuclear power plant digital twin to complete disaster response tasks. Performance metrics, physiological data, and behavioural measures were recorded to assess task performance, cognitive load, and operator awareness across conditions. The co-located shared-interface condition achieved the fastest mission completion (292.8 s), outperforming remote operation (351.6 s) and individual interfaces (385.1 s), with the fewest collisions (0.9 per trial) and highest situational awareness accuracy (91.1 %). Physical co-presence was associated with reduced cognitive load, with NASA-TLX scores increasing from 38.2 in co-located to 57.7 in remote operation, supported by consistent physiological indicators.
